   167	export function createApiKeyAuth(
   168	    env: ApiKeyAuthBindings,
   169	    ctx?: Pick<ExecutionContext, "waitUntil">,
   170	) {
   171	    const db = drizzle(env.DB);
   172	    return betterAuth({
   173	        basePath: "/api/auth",
   174	        database: drizzleAdapter(db, {
   175	            schema,
   176	            provider: "sqlite",
   177	        }),
   178	        advanced: {
   179	            backgroundTasks: ctx
   180	                ? {
   181	                      handler: (promise: Promise<unknown>) => {
   182	                          ctx.waitUntil(promise.catch(() => undefined));
   183	                      },
   184	                  }
   185	                : undefined,
   186	        },
   187	        plugins: [createApiKeyPlugin()],
   188	        telemetry: { enabled: false },
   189	    });
   190	}

   192	export function extractApiKey(request: Request): string | null {
   193	    const auth = request.headers.get("authorization");
   194	    const match = auth?.match(/^Bearer (.+)$/);
   195	    if (match?.[1]) return match[1];
   196	
   197	    // E2B's SDKs send the key in X-API-KEY.
   198	    const headerKey = request.headers.get("x-api-key");
   199	    if (headerKey) return headerKey;
   200	
   201	    // Query keys end up in access logs, referrers and browser history. Their
   202	    // owner can rotate them; agent run and session tokens cannot be revoked,
   203	    // so they are Bearer-only.
   204	    const queryKey = new URL(request.url).searchParams.get("key");
   205	    return queryKey?.startsWith(AGENT_RUN_TOKEN_PREFIX) ||
   206	        queryKey?.startsWith(SESSION_TOKEN_PREFIX)
   207	        ? null
   208	        : queryKey;
   209	}
   210	
   211	export function assertNotBanned(user: {
   212	    banned?: boolean | null;
   213	    banExpires?: Date | string | null;
   214	    banReason?: string | null;
   215	}): void {
   216	    if (!isUserBanned(user)) return;
   217	    throw new BannedAccountError(
   218	        user.banReason ? `Account banned: ${user.banReason}` : "Account banned",
   219	    );
   220	}
   221	
   222	// A key that is unknown, disabled or expired stays rejected from the cache for
   223	// this long, so a flood repeating bad keys stops reaching D1.
   224	const INVALID_KEY_CACHE_SECONDS = 300;
   225	// "Last used" is shown to the owner; minute precision is not needed, and a
   226	// write per request was most of D1's load during the 2026-10-27 floods.
   227	const LAST_REQUEST_WRITE_INTERVAL_MS = 5 * 60_000;
   228	
   229	export async function authenticateApiKeyRequest(opts: {
   230	    request: Request;
   231	    env: ApiKeyAuthBindings;
   232	    ctx?: Pick<ExecutionContext, "waitUntil">;
   233	}): Promise<ApiKeyAuthResult | null> {
   234	    const rawApiKey = extractApiKey(opts.request);
   235	    if (!rawApiKey) return null;
   236	
   237	    // pk_ keys are App Keys: public OAuth client IDs, never credentials.
   238	    if (rawApiKey.startsWith(`${PUBLISHABLE_KEY_PREFIX}_`)) {
   239	        throw new HTTPException(401, { message: PUBLISHABLE_KEY_REFUSAL });
   240	    }
   241	
   242	    if (rawApiKey.startsWith(AGENT_RUN_TOKEN_PREFIX)) {
   243	        return authenticateAgentRunToken(rawApiKey, opts.env);
   244	    }
   245	    if (rawApiKey.startsWith(SESSION_TOKEN_PREFIX)) {
   246	        return authenticateSessionToken(rawApiKey, opts.env);
   247	    }
   248	
   249	    // Better Auth's verifyApiKey does this lookup plus two awaited writes per
   250	    // call (last_request and updated_at). Our keys use none of its quota or
   251	    // rate-limit features, so look the key up by hash directly.
   252	    const keyHash = await defaultKeyHasher(rawApiKey);
   253	    const invalidKeyCacheKey = new Request(
   254	        new URL(`/__invalid-api-key/${keyHash}`, opts.request.url),
   255	    );
   256	    const invalidKeys = await caches.open("invalid-api-keys");
   257	    if (await invalidKeys.match(invalidKeyCacheKey)) return null;
   258	
   259	    const row = await selectApiKeyRow(opts.env, eq(schema.apikey.key, keyHash));
   260	    const result = toActiveAuthResult(row, rawApiKey, opts.env);
   261	    if (!result || !row) {
   262	        const remember = invalidKeys.put(
   263	            invalidKeyCacheKey,
   264	            new Response(null, {
   265	                headers: {
   266	                    "Cache-Control": `max-age=${INVALID_KEY_CACHE_SECONDS}`,
   267	                },
   268	            }),
   269	        );
   270	        runInBackground(remember, opts.ctx);
   271	        return null;
   272	    }
   273	
   274	    const lastRequest = row.apiKey.lastRequest;
   275	    const staleBefore = new Date(Date.now() - LAST_REQUEST_WRITE_INTERVAL_MS);
   276	    if (!lastRequest || lastRequest < staleBefore) {
   277	        const touch = drizzle(opts.env.DB)
   278	            .update(schema.apikey)
   279	            .set({ lastRequest: new Date() })
   280	            .where(
   281	                and(
   282	                    eq(schema.apikey.id, row.apiKey.id),
   283	                    or(
   284	                        isNull(schema.apikey.lastRequest),
   285	                        lt(schema.apikey.lastRequest, staleBefore),
   286	                    ),
   287	                ),
   288	            )
   289	            .run();
   290	        runInBackground(touch, opts.ctx);
   291	    }
   292	    return result;
   293	}
   294	
   295	function runInBackground(
   296	    promise: Promise<unknown>,
   297	    ctx?: Pick<ExecutionContext, "waitUntil">,
   298	): void {
   299	    const settled = promise.catch(() => undefined);
   300	    ctx?.waitUntil(settled);
   301	}
   302	
   303	/**
   304	 * The key row that a raw key hashes to, if it can be used: Better Auth's
   305	 * verifyApiKey checks without its per-call writes.
   306	 */
   307	export async function findUsableApiKey(
   308	    env: Pick<ApiKeyAuthBindings, "DB">,
   309	    rawKey: string,
   310	): Promise<typeof schema.apikey.$inferSelect | null> {
   311	    const row = await drizzle(env.DB, { schema }).query.apikey.findFirst({
   312	        where: eq(schema.apikey.key, await defaultKeyHasher(rawKey)),
   313	    });
   314	    if (!row || !isUsable(row)) return null;
   315	    return row;
   316	}
   317	
   318	function isUsable(key: {
   319	    enabled: boolean | null;
   320	    expiresAt: Date | null;
   321	}): boolean {
   322	    return (
   323	        key.enabled !== false && !(key.expiresAt && key.expiresAt <= new Date())
   324	    );
   325	}
   326	
   327	async function authenticateAgentRunToken(
   328	    rawToken: string,
   329	    env: ApiKeyAuthBindings,
   330	): Promise<ApiKeyAuthResult | null> {
   331	    if (!env.BETTER_AUTH_SECRET) return null;
   332	
   333	    let claims: AgentRunClaims;
   334	    try {
   335	        claims = await verifyAgentRunToken(rawToken, env.BETTER_AUTH_SECRET);
   336	    } catch {
   337	        return null;
   338	    }
   339	
   340	    const parent = await loadActiveApiKeyAuthResult({
   341	        apiKeyId: claims.parentApiKeyId,
   342	        rawApiKey: rawToken,
   343	        env,
   344	    });
   345	    if (!parent) return null;
   346	
   347	    // Agent-run tokens leave our control. Keep the parent's generation limits,
   348	    // but never let an agent manage the owner's account or keys.
   349	    const models = parent.apiKey.permissions?.models;
   350	    return {
   351	        ...parent,
   352	        apiKey: {
   353	            ...parent.apiKey,
   354	            permissions: models ? { models } : undefined,
   355	        },
   356	        agentRun: claims,
   357	    };
   358	}
   359	
   360	async function authenticateSessionToken(
   361	    rawToken: string,
   362	    env: ApiKeyAuthBindings,
   363	): Promise<ApiKeyAuthResult | null> {
   364	    if (!env.BETTER_AUTH_SECRET) return null;
   365	
   366	    let userId: string;
   367	    try {
   368	        userId = await verifySessionToken(rawToken, env.BETTER_AUTH_SECRET);
   369	    } catch {
   370	        return null;
   371	    }
   372	
   373	    const user = await drizzle(env.DB)
   374	        .select()
   375	        .from(schema.user)
   376	        .where(eq(schema.user.id, userId))
   377	        .get();
   378	    if (!user) return null;
   379	
   380	    assertNotBanned(user);
   381	    assertStagingAccess(env, user);
   382	    return { user, rawApiKey: rawToken };
   383	}
   384	
   385	/**
   386	 * Loads an active API key by ID after another credential has authenticated it.
   387	 * This deliberately does not accept the parent key's raw value so delegated
   388	 * credentials never need to contain or recover that secret.
   389	 */
   390	export async function loadActiveApiKeyAuthResult(opts: {
   391	    apiKeyId: string;
   392	    rawApiKey: string;
   393	    env: ApiKeyAuthBindings;
   394	}): Promise<(ApiKeyAuthResult & { apiKey: AuthenticatedApiKey }) | null> {
   395	    const row = await selectApiKeyRow(
   396	        opts.env,
   397	        eq(schema.apikey.id, opts.apiKeyId),
   398	    );
   399	    return toActiveAuthResult(row, opts.rawApiKey, opts.env);
   400	}
   401	
   402	type ApiKeyRow = Awaited<ReturnType<typeof selectApiKeyRow>>;
   403	
   404	async function selectApiKeyRow(env: ApiKeyAuthBindings, where: SQL) {
   405	    const db = drizzle(env.DB, { schema });
   406	    const byopClientKey = alias(schema.apikey, "byop_client_key");
   407	    const byopOwner = alias(schema.user, "byop_owner");
   408	    return db
   409	        .select({
   410	            apiKey: getTableColumns(schema.apikey),
   411	            user: getTableColumns(schema.user),
   412	            byopClientName: byopClientKey.name,
   413	            byopOwner: {
   414	                banned: byopOwner.banned,
   415	                banExpires: byopOwner.banExpires,
   416	            },
   417	            byopClientUserId: byopClientKey.referenceId,
   418	            byopClientPrefix: byopClientKey.prefix,
   419	            byopClientEnabled: byopClientKey.enabled,
   420	            byopClientExpiresAt: byopClientKey.expiresAt,
   421	            byopClientMetadata: byopClientKey.metadata,
   422	        })
   423	        .from(schema.apikey)
   424	        .innerJoin(schema.user, eq(schema.user.id, schema.apikey.referenceId))
   425	        .leftJoin(
   426	            byopClientKey,
   427	            eq(byopClientKey.id, schema.apikey.byopClientKeyId),
   428	        )
   429	        .where(where)
   430	        .leftJoin(byopOwner, eq(byopOwner.id, byopClientKey.referenceId))
   431	        .get();
   432	}
   433	
   434	function toActiveAuthResult(
   435	    row: ApiKeyRow,
   436	    rawApiKey: string,
   437	    env: ApiKeyAuthBindings,
   438	): (ApiKeyAuthResult & { apiKey: AuthenticatedApiKey }) | null {
   439	    if (!row || !isUsable(row.apiKey)) return null;
   440	    // The stored type, not the prefix: older App Keys look like plln_pk_….
   441	    const metadata = normalizeMetadata(parseMetadata(row.apiKey.metadata));
   442	    if (metadata?.keyType === "publishable") {
   443	        throw new HTTPException(401, { message: PUBLISHABLE_KEY_REFUSAL });
   444	    }
   445	
   446	    assertNotBanned(row.user);
   447	    if (row.byopOwner) assertNotBanned(row.byopOwner);
   448	    assertStagingAccess(env, row.user);
   449	
   450	    return {
   451	        user: row.user,
   452	        apiKey: {
   453	            id: row.apiKey.id,
   454	            name: row.apiKey.name ?? undefined,
   455	            permissions: normalizePermissions(
   456	                parseMetadata(row.apiKey.permissions),
   457	            ),
   458	            metadata,
   459	            pollenBalance: row.apiKey.pollenBalance ?? null,
   460	            expiresAt: row.apiKey.expiresAt,
   461	            questPollenOnly: row.apiKey.questPollenOnly,
   462	            byopClientKeyId: row.apiKey.byopClientKeyId ?? null,
   463	            byopClientName: row.byopClientName ?? null,
   464	            byopClientUserId: row.byopClientUserId ?? null,
   465	            byopMarkupApplies: byopClientAllowsMarkup(
   466	                {
   467	                    userId: row.byopClientUserId,
   468	                    prefix: row.byopClientPrefix,
   469	                    enabled: row.byopClientEnabled,
   470	                    expiresAt: row.byopClientExpiresAt,
   471	                    metadata: row.byopClientMetadata,
   472	                },
   473	                row.user.id,
   474	            ),
   475	            rawKey: rawApiKey,
   476	        },
   477	        rawApiKey,
   478	    };
   479	}
   480	
   481	function normalizePermissions(
   482	    value: unknown,
   483	): Record<string, string[]> | undefined {
   484	    if (!value || typeof value !== "object" || Array.isArray(value)) {
   485	        return undefined;
   486	    }
   487	
   488	    const permissions: Record<string, string[]> = {};
   489	    for (const [key, scopes] of Object.entries(value)) {
   490	        if (!Array.isArray(scopes)) continue;
   491	        const safeScopes = scopes.filter(
   492	            (scope): scope is string => typeof scope === "string",
   493	        );
   494	        if (safeScopes.length || key === "models") {
   495	            permissions[key] = safeScopes;
   496	        }
   497	    }
   498	    return Object.keys(permissions).length ? permissions : undefined;
   499	}
   500	
   501	function normalizeMetadata(
   502	    value: unknown,
   503	): Record<string, unknown> | undefined {
   504	    if (!value || typeof value !== "object" || Array.isArray(value)) {
   505	        return undefined;
   506	    }
   507	    return value as Record<string, unknown>;
   508	}

     6	/**
     7	 * Parse a scope/permissions URL parameter. Accepts both OAuth-canonical
     8	 * space-separated format (`scope=usage%20keys`) and our legacy
     9	 * comma-separated format (`permissions=usage,keys`).

    11	export function parseScopeList(val: unknown): string[] | null {
    12	    if (typeof val !== "string" || !val) return null;
    13	    const items = val
    14	        .split(/[\s,]+/)
    15	        .map((s) => s.trim())
    16	        .filter(Boolean);
    17	    return items.length ? items : null;

    35	export const DEFAULT_CONSENT_BUDGET = 5;
    36	export const DEFAULT_CONSENT_EXPIRY_DAYS = 7;
    37	/** The most budget a link can pre-fill; the user can raise it by hand. */
    38	export const MAX_LINK_CONSENT_BUDGET = 10;

    40	const SECONDS_PER_DAY = 24 * 60 * 60;
    41	
    42	/**
    43	 * The expiry field is in days and accepts fractions, but key creation takes
    44	 * whole seconds (`z.number().int().positive()`), so a fraction landing
    45	 * mid-second failed validation. Rounding is the whole fix.
    46	 *
    47	 * An empty field is the only thing that means "no expiry". Anything invalid
    48	 * stays invalid and the server rejects it, which the dialogs surface.
    49	 */
    50	export function expiryDaysToExpiresIn(
    51	    expiryDays: number | null | undefined,
    52	): number | undefined {
    53	    if (expiryDays == null) return undefined;
    54	    return Math.round(expiryDays * SECONDS_PER_DAY);
    55	}

    57	/**
    58	 * An S256 PKCE code_challenge is exactly 43 base64url chars (unpadded
    59	 * SHA-256, RFC 7636 §4.2). Single source of truth for the consent page's
    60	 * front-door check and the server's CreateCodeSchema.
    61	 */
    62	export const PKCE_S256_CHALLENGE_REGEX = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/;

    64	/**
    65	 * Account permissions the user can grant at the consent screen. Every scope is
    66	 * opt-in — nothing is implicit. A caller's own key metadata (`/account/key`),
    67	 * its budget, its usage (`/account/key/usage`), and the user's github username +
    68	 * image (`/account/profile`) are all readable without any scope.
    69	 *
    70	 * - `profile`: read account name and email
    71	 * - `usage`: read full account balance + account-wide usage (key's own
    72	 *   balance and usage are free regardless)
    73	 * - `keys`: account admin; create, list, and revoke API keys, plus My Models
    74	 *   access where enabled.
    75	 * - `machines`: create and run hosted sandboxes.
    76	 */
    77	export const CONSENT_PERMISSIONS = [
    78	    "profile",
    79	    "usage",
    80	    "keys",
    81	    "machines",
    82	] as const;
    83	
    84	export const OAUTH_SCOPES = ["generate", ...CONSENT_PERMISSIONS] as const;
    85	
    86	/** Generation is inherent to API keys; account scopes remain opt-in. */
    87	export function getGrantedOAuthScope(
    88	    requested: ReadonlySet<string>,
    89	    accountPermissions: string[],
    90	): string | undefined {
    91	    if (!requested.size) return undefined;
    92	    return [
    93	        ...(requested.has("generate") ? ["generate"] : []),
    94	        ...accountPermissions,
    95	    ].join(" ");
    96	}
    97	
    98	export function sanitizeAuthorizeAccountPermissions(
    99	    permissions: string[] | null | undefined,
   100	): string[] | null {
   101	    if (!permissions?.length) return null;
   102	
   103	    const filtered = Array.from(
   104	        new Set(
   105	            permissions.filter((permission) =>
   106	                CONSENT_PERMISSIONS.includes(
   107	                    permission as (typeof CONSENT_PERMISSIONS)[number],
   108	                ),
   109	            ),
   110	        ),
   111	    );
   112	
   113	    return filtered.length ? filtered : null;
   114	}
   115	
   116	/**
   117	 * Most people click "Allow" without reading, so a link can request `keys` and
   118	 * `machines` but never tick them: the user has to grant those on purpose.
   119	 */
   120	const DELIBERATE_CONSENT_PERMISSIONS: readonly string[] = ["keys", "machines"];
   121	
   122	/** The requested account permissions the consent screen starts with ticked. */
   123	export function getPreselectedConsentPermissions(
   124	    permissions: string[] | null | undefined,
   125	): string[] | null {
   126	    const preselected = sanitizeAuthorizeAccountPermissions(
   127	        permissions,
   128	    )?.filter(
   129	        (permission) => !DELIBERATE_CONSENT_PERMISSIONS.includes(permission),
   130	    );
   131	    return preselected?.length ? preselected : null;
   132	}
   133	
   134	/** A redirect to this computer, e.g. a local MCP client such as Claude Code. */
   135	function isLoopbackRedirect(url: URL | null): boolean {
   136	    return url?.protocol === "http:" && isLoopbackHostname(url.hostname);
   137	}
   138	
   139	/**
   140	 * The requested permissions the consent screen offers. `keys` (account admin)
   141	 * is only offered in the device flow (polli) and on redirects to this computer
   142	 * (local MCP clients such as Claude Code): a phished link that redirects to a
   143	 * website must never get it.
   144	 */
   145	export function getConsentPermissionChoices(
   146	    requested: ReadonlySet<string>,
   147	    isDeviceFlow: boolean,
   148	    redirectUrl: URL | null,
   149	): string[] {
   150	    const offersKeys = isDeviceFlow || isLoopbackRedirect(redirectUrl);
   151	    return CONSENT_PERMISSIONS.filter(
   152	        (permission) =>
   153	            requested.has(permission) && (offersKeys || permission !== "keys"),
   154	    );
   155	}
   156	
   157	/**
   158	 * Whether a grant link may add `keys` to an existing key. Same rule as the
   159	 * consent screen: never to a key an app got by redirecting to a website. Keys
   160	 * from polli's device login, the dashboard or the API have no redirect origin.
   161	 */
   162	export function canGrantKeysByLink(redirectOrigin: unknown): boolean {
   163	    if (redirectOrigin === undefined) return true;
   164	    return (
   165	        typeof redirectOrigin === "string" &&
   166	        isLoopbackRedirect(parseAuthorizeRedirectUrl(redirectOrigin))
   167	    );
   168	}
   169	
   170	export function getAuthorizeInitialPermissions({
   171	    models,
   172	    budget,
   173	    expiry,
   174	    permissions,
   175	}: AuthorizeDefaultsInput) {
   176	    return {
   177	        allowedModels: models,
   178	        pollenBudget: Math.max(
   179	            0,
   180	            Math.min(budget ?? DEFAULT_CONSENT_BUDGET, MAX_LINK_CONSENT_BUDGET),
   181	        ),
   182	        expiryDays: expiry ?? DEFAULT_CONSENT_EXPIRY_DAYS,
   183	        accountPermissions: getPreselectedConsentPermissions(permissions),
   184	    };
   185	}

   100	/**
   101	 * Parse a comma-separated list of numeric GitHub user IDs.
   102	 * Strict: only entries matching /^\d+$/ are kept, so "123abc" is dropped
   103	 * instead of being silently truncated to 123.
   104	 */
   105	export function parseGithubIdList(raw: string | undefined | null): Set<number> {
   106	    if (!raw) return new Set();
   107	    const ids = new Set<number>();
   108	    for (const part of raw.split(",")) {
   109	        const trimmed = part.trim();
   110	        if (!/^\d+$/.test(trimmed)) continue;
   111	        const n = Number(trimmed);
   112	        if (n > 0) ids.add(n);
   113	    }
   114	    return ids;
   115	}

===== shared/auth/redirect-uri.ts =====
     1	/**
     2	 * Match an incoming `redirect_uri` against a registered allowlist for a `pk_`.
     3	 *
     4	 * Scheme policy (https-only except loopback http) is enforced at registration
     5	 * time (see validateRedirectUriFormat). Matching trusts the stored allowlist
     6	 * and does not re-check the scheme.
     7	 *
     8	 * Comparison rules:
     9	 * - Scheme + hostname + path are matched exactly (after lowercasing host).
    10	 * - Trailing slash on the path is insignificant: `/cb` and `/cb/` match.
    11	 * - Query strings are ignored when the registered URI has no query: apps
    12	 *   round-trip state (e.g. `?prompt=...`) and the auth code/token rides the URL
    13	 *   fragment, not the query. If the registered URI includes a query, it must
    14	 *   match exactly so existing query-bound allowlist entries are not broadened.
    15	 * - For loopback entries (RFC 8252 §7.3): port is ignored — any port matches.
    16	 *   This covers native/CLI apps that bind to ephemeral ports each run.
    17	 * - For non-loopback entries: port must match (default ports normalized).
    18	 * - Fragments are rejected; redirect URIs must not contain them.
    19	 *
    20	 * Returns false on any parse error or empty allowlist.
    21	 *
    22	 * Single source of truth for both /api/app-lookup (consent screen attribution)
    23	 * and createApiKeyForUser (sk_ minting). Keep them aligned.
    24	 */
    25	export function redirectUriMatchesAllowlist(
    26	    uri: string,
    27	    allowlist: readonly string[] | null | undefined,
    28	): boolean {
    29	    if (!allowlist?.length) return false;
    30	    const incoming = safeParse(uri);
    31	    if (!incoming) return false;
    32	    return allowlist.some((entry) => matchesEntry(incoming, entry));
    33	}
    34	
    35	/**
    36	 * Strict variant for the OAuth authorization-code flow (RFC 6749 §3.1.2.3):
    37	 * the authorization code rides the redirect query string, so the fragment-era
    38	 * leniency of accepting extra query params must not apply. The query must
    39	 * equal the registered entry's exactly (normally: both absent). Loopback
    40	 * ports stay port-agnostic (RFC 8252 §7.3) and one trailing slash is still
    41	 * ignored. The legacy fragment flow keeps the lenient matcher above.
    42	 */
    43	export function redirectUriMatchesAllowlistExact(
    44	    uri: string,
    45	    allowlist: readonly string[] | null | undefined,
    46	): boolean {
    47	    if (!allowlist?.length) return false;
    48	    const incoming = safeParse(uri);
    49	    if (!incoming) return false;
    50	    return allowlist.some((entry) => matchesEntry(incoming, entry, true));
    51	}
    52	
    53	// Schemes the browser handles itself. Sending the consent page to one would
    54	// load or run it on this page instead of handing the result back to an app.
    55	const BROWSER_SCHEMES = new Set([
    56	    "javascript:",
    57	    "data:",
    58	    "vbscript:",
    59	    "file:",
    60	    "blob:",
    61	    "about:",
    62	    "filesystem:",
    63	]);
    64	
    65	/**
    66	 * Parse the redirect target of the consent screen: a website, a loopback
    67	 * server or a native app's own scheme (e.g. `myapp://callback`). Null when the
    68	 * URL is unparseable or uses a scheme the browser handles itself, so such a
    69	 * target never reaches window.location. The URL parser normalizes the scheme,
    70	 * and callers navigate to the parsed URL, so case or whitespace tricks in the
    71	 * raw string cannot slip past the check.
    72	 */
    73	export function parseAuthorizeRedirectUrl(url: string): URL | null {
    74	    const parsed = safeParse(url);
    75	    return parsed && !BROWSER_SCHEMES.has(parsed.protocol) ? parsed : null;
    76	}
    77	
    78	export function isAllowedRedirectUrl(url: URL): boolean {
    79	    if (url.protocol === "https:") return true;
    80	    return url.protocol === "http:" && isLoopbackHostname(url.hostname);
    81	}
    82	
    83	export function isLoopbackHostname(hostname: string): boolean {
    84	    const h = normalizeHostname(hostname);
    85	    if (h === "localhost" || h === "0.0.0.0" || h === "::1") return true;
    86	    if (/^127\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+$/.test(h)) return true;
    87	    return false;
    88	}
    89	
    90	function safeParse(url: string): URL | null {
    91	    try {
    92	        return new URL(url);
    93	    } catch {
    94	        return null;
    95	    }
    96	}
    97	
    98	function normalizeHostname(hostname: string): string {
    99	    return hostname
   100	        .toLowerCase()
   101	        .replace(/^\[(.*)\]$/, "$1")
   102	        .replace(/\.$/, "");
   103	}
   104	
   105	function normalizePathname(pathname: string): string {
   106	    return pathname.length > 1 && pathname.endsWith("/")
   107	        ? pathname.slice(0, -1)
   108	        : pathname;
   109	}
   110	
   111	function matchesEntry(
   112	    incoming: URL,
   113	    entryUrl: string,
   114	    exactQuery = false,
   115	): boolean {
   116	    const entry = safeParse(entryUrl);
   117	    if (!entry) return false;
   118	    if (incoming.hash || entry.hash) return false;
   119	    if (incoming.protocol !== entry.protocol) return false;
   120	    if (
   121	        normalizeHostname(incoming.hostname) !==
   122	        normalizeHostname(entry.hostname)
   123	    ) {
   124	        return false;
   125	    }
   126	    if (
   127	        normalizePathname(incoming.pathname) !==
   128	        normalizePathname(entry.pathname)
   129	    ) {
   130	        return false;
   131	    }
   132	    if (exactQuery) {
   133	        if (incoming.search !== entry.search) return false;
   134	    } else if (entry.search && incoming.search !== entry.search) {
   135	        return false;
   136	    }
   137	    if (isLoopbackHostname(entry.hostname)) return true;
   138	    return incoming.port === entry.port;
   139	}
===== shared/auth/session-token.ts =====
     1	import { jwtVerify, SignJWT } from "jose";
     2	
     3	// A short-lived bearer credential the Enter dashboard mints from its session
     4	// cookie, so the dashboard calls the public API like any other client instead
     5	// of keeping cookie-only copies of the same routes. It acts as the account
     6	// owner with no key restrictions. It is not tied to the cookie session:
     7	// signing out leaves it valid until it expires.
     8	export const SESSION_TOKEN_PREFIX = "sess_";
     9	export const SESSION_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = 900;
    10	
    11	const SESSION_TOKEN_ISSUER = "enter.pollinations.ai";
    12	const SESSION_TOKEN_AUDIENCE = "pollinations-api";
    13	const MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_SECONDS = 5;
    14	
    15	function signingKey(secret: string) {
    16	    return new TextEncoder().encode(`pollinations-session-token:v1\0${secret}`);
    17	}
    18	
    19	export async function signSessionToken(opts: {
    20	    secret: string;
    21	    userId: string;
    22	    now?: number;
    23	}): Promise<string> {
    24	    const issuedAt = opts.now ?? Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
    25	    const token = await new SignJWT({})
    26	        .setProtectedHeader({ alg: "HS256", typ: "JWT" })
    27	        .setIssuer(SESSION_TOKEN_ISSUER)
    28	        .setAudience(SESSION_TOKEN_AUDIENCE)
    29	        .setSubject(opts.userId)
    30	        .setIssuedAt(issuedAt)
    31	        .setExpirationTime(issuedAt + SESSION_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS)
    32	        .sign(signingKey(opts.secret));
    33	    return `${SESSION_TOKEN_PREFIX}${token}`;
    34	}
    35	
    36	/**
    37	 * Returns the user id a `sess_` token was minted for. Throws if it is
    38	 * invalid. Callers check the prefix.
    39	 */
    40	export async function verifySessionToken(
    41	    token: string,
    42	    secret: string,
    43	): Promise<string> {
    44	    const { payload } = await jwtVerify(
    45	        token.slice(SESSION_TOKEN_PREFIX.length),
    46	        signingKey(secret),
    47	        {
    48	            algorithms: ["HS256"],
    49	            issuer: SESSION_TOKEN_ISSUER,
    50	            audience: SESSION_TOKEN_AUDIENCE,
    51	            clockTolerance: MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_SECONDS,
    52	            typ: "JWT",
    53	            requiredClaims: ["exp", "sub"],
    54	        },
    55	    );
    56	    if (typeof payload.sub !== "string" || !payload.sub) {
    57	        throw new Error("Invalid session token subject");
    58	    }
    59	    return payload.sub;
    60	}

    36	/**
    37	 * Get the total positive balance across relevant buckets.
    38	 * For paid-only models: pack only.
    39	 */
    40	export function getAvailableBalance(
    41	    balances: UserBalance,
    42	    isPaidOnly = false,
    43	): number {
    44	    if (isPaidOnly || balances.questPollenRestricted) {
    45	        return Math.max(0, balances.packBalance);
    46	    }
    47	    return (
    48	        Math.max(0, balances.tierBalance) + Math.max(0, balances.packBalance)
    49	    );
    50	}

    52	/**
    53	 * Map a deduction bucket to its meter id/slug pair. The balances sub-object
    54	 * differs per call site, so this returns only the id/slug pair.
    55	 */
    56	export function payerBucketToMeter(bucket: BalanceBucket): {
    57	    selectedMeterId: string;
    58	    selectedMeterSlug: "v1:meter:tier" | "v1:meter:pack";
    59	} {
    60	    return {
    61	        selectedMeterId: `local:${bucket}`,
    62	        selectedMeterSlug:
    63	            bucket === "tier" ? "v1:meter:tier" : "v1:meter:pack",
    64	    };
    65	}
    66	
    67	export function createBalanceCheckResult(
    68	    balances: UserBalance,
    69	    isPaidOnly = false,
    70	): BalanceCheckResult {
    71	    isPaidOnly ||= balances.questPollenRestricted === true;
    72	    // Which bucket the charge is expected to land in, for the reported meter.
    73	    // The authoritative choice is the SQL ladder in atomicDeductUserBalance.
    74	    const source: BalanceBucket = isPaidOnly
    75	        ? "pack"
    76	        : balances.tierBalance > 0
    77	          ? "tier"
    78	          : "pack";
    79	    return {
    80	        ...payerBucketToMeter(source),
    81	        balances: {
    82	            "v1:meter:tier": isPaidOnly ? 0 : balances.tierBalance,
    83	            "v1:meter:pack": balances.packBalance,
    84	        },
    85	    };
    86	}
===== shared/billing/bucket-selection.ts =====
     1	export type UserBalance = {
     2	    tierBalance: number;
     3	    packBalance: number;
     4	    questPollenRestricted?: boolean;
     5	};
     6	
     7	export type BalanceBucket = "tier" | "pack";
     8	
     9	/**
    10	 * Preflight "can the caller afford this estimate" check. This is intentionally
    11	 * a different question from the authoritative bucket ladder in
    12	 * `atomicDeductUserBalance`: that function chooses *which* bucket to write to
    13	 * when money actually moves; this one only asks whether *enough exists* to let
    14	 * the request proceed before any mutation.
    15	 *
    16	 * The two therefore need not use identical thresholds. This preflight clamps
    17	 * negative estimates to zero, but every request still requires a positive
    18	 * balance in at least one bucket. The write path skips non-positive charges
    19	 * entirely; for a positive actual charge, it uses
    20	 * Quest Pollen when that bucket covers the charge, otherwise any positive paid
    21	 * balance, and finally Quest Pollen debt when the paid balance is non-positive.
    22	 */
    23	export function canCoverEstimatedCharge(
    24	    balances: UserBalance,
    25	    estimatedCost: number,
    26	    isPaidOnly = false,
    27	): boolean {
    28	    const tierBalance = balances.questPollenRestricted
    29	        ? 0
    30	        : balances.tierBalance;
    31	    const hasPositiveBalance = tierBalance > 0 || balances.packBalance > 0;
    32	    if (!hasPositiveBalance) return false;
    33	
    34	    const threshold = Math.max(0, estimatedCost);
    35	    // Paid-only stays strict: the flag means "must hold paid balance", a
    36	    // positive-balance requirement rather than a cost-coverage one. A paid-only
    37	    // model is never free, so no zero-balance caller needs to get through.
    38	    if (isPaidOnly) return balances.packBalance > threshold;
    39	    // Once the wallet has a positive bucket, compare each bucket to the cost.
    40	    return tierBalance >= threshold || balances.packBalance >= threshold;
    41	}
===== shared/billing/deduction.ts =====
     1	import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
     2	import type { DrizzleD1Database } from "drizzle-orm/d1";
     3	import { apikey as apiKeyTable, user as userTable } from "../db/better-auth.ts";
     4	import type { BalanceBucket, UserBalance } from "./bucket-selection.ts";
     5	import { POLLEN_BILLING_PRECISION } from "./precision.ts";
     6	
     7	export type Bucket = BalanceBucket;
     8	
     9	const BUCKET_COLUMNS = {
    10	    tier: userTable.tierBalance,
    11	    pack: userTable.packBalance,
    12	} as const satisfies Record<Bucket, unknown>;
    13	
    14	/**
    15	 * Atomically deducts pollen from user balance.
    16	 *
    17	 * This is the authoritative deduction ladder — the one place a positive charge
    18	 * picks a bucket and money actually moves, read top-to-bottom as the `decision`
    19	 * CASE below. `canCoverEstimatedCharge` answers the separate preflight question
    20	 * of whether an estimate is affordable, while `createBalanceCheckResult` only
    21	 * labels a meter for reporting. Neither is an authoritative write-path rule.
    22	 *
    23	 *   1. paid-only  → `pack` only (never Quest Pollen)
    24	 *   2. quest-only → `tier` only, for keys that never spend paid Pollen
    25	 *   3. restricted → `pack`, including debt for requests already admitted
    26	 *   4. tier       → Quest Pollen when it covers the full amount (`>=`)
    27	 *   5. pack       → any positive paid balance when Quest Pollen can't cover
    28	 *   6. tier       → fall back to Quest Pollen when pack is non-positive
    29	 *
    30	 * The final `tier` fall-through is load-bearing: when Quest Pollen cannot cover
    31	 * the charge and paid balance is non-positive, the charge accrues Quest-Pollen
    32	 * debt instead of reducing paid balance further. Non-positive amounts return
    33	 * without selecting a bucket or writing.
    34	 * Restrictions reject new Quest-only requests at preflight. Those already in
    35	 * flight still settle in their permitted bucket; completed work is never free.
    36	 */
    37	export async function atomicDeductUserBalance(
    38	    db: DrizzleD1Database,
    39	    userId: string,
    40	    amount: number,
    41	    isPaidOnly = false,
    42	    questPollenOnly = false,
    43	): Promise<{
    44	    ok: boolean;
    45	    bucket: Bucket | null;
    46	    packBalance: number | null;
    47	    lastPackPollen: number | null;
    48	    postDeductionBalance: number | null;
    49	}> {
    50	    if (amount <= 0) {
    51	        return {
    52	            ok: true,
    53	            bucket: null,
    54	            packBalance: null,
    55	            lastPackPollen: null,
    56	            postDeductionBalance: null,
    57	        };
    58	    }
    59	
    60	    const row = await db.get<{
    61	        bucket: Bucket;
    62	        tierBalance: number | null;
    63	        packBalance: number | null;
    64	        lastPackPollen: number | null;
    65	    }>(
    66	        sql`
    67	        WITH decision AS MATERIALIZED (
    68	            SELECT
    69	                id,
    70	                CASE
    71	                    WHEN ${isPaidOnly ? 1 : 0} = 1 THEN 'pack'
    72	                    WHEN ${questPollenOnly ? 1 : 0} = 1 THEN 'tier'
    73	                    WHEN quest_pollen_restricted = 1 THEN 'pack'
    74	                    WHEN COALESCE(tier_balance, 0) >= ${amount} THEN 'tier'
    75	                    WHEN COALESCE(pack_balance, 0) > 0 THEN 'pack'
    76	                    ELSE 'tier'
    77	                END AS bucket
    78	            FROM ${userTable}
    79	            WHERE id = ${userId}
    80	        )
    81	        UPDATE ${userTable}
    82	        SET
    83	            tier_balance = CASE
    84	                WHEN (SELECT bucket FROM decision) = 'tier'
    85	                    THEN ROUND(COALESCE(tier_balance, 0) - ${amount}, ${POLLEN_BILLING_PRECISION})
    86	                ELSE tier_balance
    87	            END,
    88	            pack_balance = CASE
    89	                WHEN (SELECT bucket FROM decision) = 'pack'
    90	                    THEN ROUND(COALESCE(pack_balance, 0) - ${amount}, ${POLLEN_BILLING_PRECISION})
    91	                ELSE pack_balance
    92	            END
    93	        WHERE id = (SELECT id FROM decision)
    94	        RETURNING
    95	            (SELECT bucket FROM decision) AS bucket,
    96	            tier_balance AS tierBalance,
    97	            pack_balance AS packBalance,
    98	            last_pack_pollen AS lastPackPollen
    99	    `,
   100	    );
   101	
   102	    return {
   103	        ok: !!row,
   104	        bucket: row?.bucket ?? null,
   105	        packBalance: row?.packBalance ?? null,
   106	        lastPackPollen: row?.lastPackPollen ?? null,
   107	        postDeductionBalance: row
   108	            ? row.bucket === "tier"
   109	                ? row.tierBalance
   110	                : row.packBalance
   111	            : null,
   112	    };
   113	}
   114	
   115	/** Reserve an estimated charge from a finite API-key budget. */
   116	export async function atomicReserveApiKeyBalance(
   117	    db: DrizzleD1Database,
   118	    apiKeyId: string,
   119	    amount: number,
   120	): Promise<{ ok: boolean; reserved: number }> {
   121	    if (amount <= 0) return { ok: true, reserved: 0 };
   122	
   123	    const result = await db.run(sql`
   124				UPDATE ${apiKeyTable}
   125				SET pollen_balance = ROUND(pollen_balance - ${amount}, ${POLLEN_BILLING_PRECISION})
   126				WHERE id = ${apiKeyId}
   127				AND pollen_balance IS NOT NULL
   128				AND pollen_balance >= ${amount}
   129			`);
   130	
   131	    const ok = (result.meta.changes ?? 0) > 0;
   132	    return { ok, reserved: ok ? amount : 0 };
   133	}
   134	
   135	/**
   136	 * Reconcile a finite API-key budget with the final charge. Positive amounts
   137	 * deduct more; negative amounts release unused reservation.
   138	 */
   139	export async function atomicAdjustApiKeyBalance(
   140	    db: DrizzleD1Database,
   141	    apiKeyId: string,
   142	    amount: number,
   143	): Promise<{ ok: boolean }> {
   144	    if (amount === 0) return { ok: true };
   145	
   146	    const result = await db.run(sql`
   147				UPDATE ${apiKeyTable}
   148				SET pollen_balance = ROUND(pollen_balance - ${amount}, ${POLLEN_BILLING_PRECISION})
   149				WHERE id = ${apiKeyId}
   150				AND pollen_balance IS NOT NULL
   151			`);
   152	
   153	    return { ok: (result.meta.changes ?? 0) > 0 };
   154	}
   155	
   156	export type { UserBalance };
   157	
   158	/**
   159	 * Atomically credits a positive amount to a user balance bucket.
   160	 */
   161	export async function atomicCreditUserBalance(
   162	    db: DrizzleD1Database,
   163	    userId: string,
   164	    bucket: Bucket,
   165	    amount: number,
   166	): Promise<{ ok: boolean; newBalance: number | null }> {
   167	    if (amount <= 0) return { ok: true, newBalance: null };
   168	
   169	    const column = BUCKET_COLUMNS[bucket];
   170	    const rows = await db
   171	        .update(userTable)
   172	        .set({
   173	            [`${bucket}Balance`]: sql`ROUND(COALESCE(${column}, 0) + ${amount}, ${POLLEN_BILLING_PRECISION})`,
   174	        })
   175	        .where(sql`${userTable.id} = ${userId}`)
   176	        .returning({ newBalance: column });
   177	
   178	    return {
   179	        ok: rows.length > 0,
   180	        newBalance: rows[0]?.newBalance ?? null,
   181	    };
   182	}
===== shared/billing/internal-automation.ts =====
     1	import type { DrizzleD1Database } from "drizzle-orm/d1";
     2	import { getUserBalance, type UserBalance } from "./balance.ts";
     3	
     4	// The one Pollinations-owned account used by GitHub automation.
     5	export const INTERNAL_AUTOMATION_USER_ID = "LJVtOPiUl0C4uRku8kL8prpp95m8jLnt";
     6	
     7	const REFILL_AT_POLLEN = 10;
     8	const QUEST_TARGET_POLLEN = 100;
     9	const PAID_TARGET_POLLEN = 20;
    10	
    11	export function isInternalAutomationAccount(userId: string): boolean {
    12	    return userId === INTERNAL_AUTOMATION_USER_ID;
    13	}
    14	
    15	/** Refill before preflight, including when the account has reached zero. */
    16	export async function getFundedUserBalance(
    17	    db: DrizzleD1Database,
    18	    d1: D1Database,
    19	    userId: string,
    20	): Promise<UserBalance> {
    21	    const balance = await getUserBalance(db, userId);
    22	    if (!isInternalAutomationAccount(userId)) {
    23	        return balance;
    24	    }
    25	
    26	    const refills = [
    27	        {
    28	            bucket: "tier",
    29	            column: "tier_balance",
    30	            title: "Internal automation Quest credit",
    31	            balance: balance.tierBalance,
    32	            target: QUEST_TARGET_POLLEN,
    33	        },
    34	        {
    35	            bucket: "pack",
    36	            column: "pack_balance",
    37	            title: "Internal automation Paid credit",
    38	            balance: balance.packBalance,
    39	            target: PAID_TARGET_POLLEN,
    40	        },
    41	    ].filter(({ balance }) => balance <= REFILL_AT_POLLEN);
    42	    if (refills.length === 0) return balance;
    43	
    44	    // D1 batch is a transaction. A concurrent request rechecks the balance
    45	    // after the first refill and cannot record or apply a second grant.
    46	    await d1.batch(
    47	        refills.flatMap(({ bucket, column, title, target }) => {
    48	            const grantId = crypto.randomUUID();
    49	            return [
    50	                d1
    51	                    .prepare(
    52	                        `INSERT INTO rewards (
    53	                id, idempotency_key, user_id, quest_id, title,
    54	                pollen_amount, balance_bucket, earned_at, claimed_at
    55	            )
    56	            SELECT ?, ?, id, NULL, ?,
    57	                ROUND(? - COALESCE(${column}, 0), 8),
    58	                ?, unixepoch(), unixepoch()
    59	            FROM user
    60	            WHERE id = ?
    61	                AND COALESCE(${column}, 0) <= ?`,
    62	                    )
    63	                    .bind(
    64	                        grantId,
    65	                        `internal-automation:${bucket}:${grantId}`,
    66	                        title,
    67	                        target,
    68	                        bucket,
    69	                        userId,
    70	                        REFILL_AT_POLLEN,
    71	                    ),
    72	                d1
    73	                    .prepare(
    74	                        `UPDATE user
    75	            SET ${column} = ROUND(COALESCE(${column}, 0) +
    76	                (SELECT pollen_amount FROM rewards WHERE id = ?), 8)
    77	            WHERE id = ? AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM rewards WHERE id = ?)`,
    78	                    )
    79	                    .bind(grantId, userId, grantId),
    80	            ];
    81	        }),
    82	    );
    83	
    84	    return getUserBalance(db, userId);
    85	}
===== shared/billing/markup.ts =====
     1	import { parseMetadata } from "../auth/api-key-metadata.ts";
     2	import { roundPollenLedgerAmount } from "./precision.ts";
     3	
     4	/**
     5	 * BYOP markup applied to requests authenticated by a BYOP-issued sk_ token with
     6	 * a trusted byop_client_key_id. The payer is billed baseline + markup; the
     7	 * markup is credited to the app owner's matching Quest Pollen or pack balance.
     8	 */
     9	export const MARKUP_PCT = 0.25;
    10	
    11	export function computeDevCredit(baselinePrice: number): number {
    12	    if (baselinePrice <= 0 || MARKUP_PCT <= 0) return 0;
    13	    return baselinePrice * MARKUP_PCT;
    14	}
    15	
    16	export type ByopClientMarkupFields = {
    17	    userId?: string | null;
    18	    prefix?: string | null;
    19	    enabled?: boolean | null;
    20	    expiresAt?: Date | string | null;
    21	    metadata?: string | Record<string, unknown> | null;
    22	};
    23	
    24	/**
    25	 * Same eligibility `resolveDevMarkup` uses after its D1 lookup. Auth computes
    26	 * this from the already-joined publishable key so preflight can include markup
    27	 * without a second query.
    28	 */
    29	export function byopClientAllowsMarkup(
    30	    client: ByopClientMarkupFields | null | undefined,
    31	    payerUserId: string | undefined,
    32	): boolean {
    33	    if (!client?.userId || !payerUserId) return false;
    34	    if (client.prefix !== "pk") return false;
    35	    if (client.enabled !== true) return false;
    36	    if (client.expiresAt && new Date(client.expiresAt) <= new Date()) {
    37	        return false;
    38	    }
    39	    const metadata =
    40	        typeof client.metadata === "string"
    41	            ? parseMetadata(client.metadata)
    42	            : (client.metadata ?? {});
    43	    if (metadata.earningsEnabled !== true) return false;
    44	    return client.userId !== payerUserId;
    45	}
    46	
    47	/** Baseline plus BYOP markup, rounded the same way deduction bills. */
    48	export function withByopMarkup(
    49	    baselinePrice: number,
    50	    applies: boolean,
    51	): number {
    52	    const baseline = Math.max(0, baselinePrice);
    53	    if (!applies) return baseline;
    54	    return roundPollenLedgerAmount(baseline + computeDevCredit(baseline));
    55	}
===== shared/billing/precision.ts =====
     1	/**
     2	 * Pollen billing precision policy.
     3	 *
     4	 * The smallest billable Pollen unit is 1e-8. Ledger debits, credits, and
     5	 * analytics totals round to this precision so they agree exactly.
     6	 */
     7	export const POLLEN_BILLING_PRECISION = 8;
     8	
     9	export function roundPollenLedgerAmount(amount: number): number {
    10	    if (!Number.isFinite(amount)) {
    11	        throw new RangeError("Pollen ledger amount must be finite");
    12	    }
    13	    const factor = 10 ** POLLEN_BILLING_PRECISION;
    14	    const rounded = Math.round(amount * factor) / factor;
    15	    // Collapse the `-0` that Math.round produces for sub-precision negatives
    16	    // into `+0`. Ledger amounts are unsigned-equivalent at the boundary.
    17	    return rounded === 0 ? 0 : rounded;
    18	}
===== shared/billing/rewards.ts =====
     1	import { and, eq, isNull, sql } from "drizzle-orm";
     2	import type { DrizzleD1Database } from "drizzle-orm/d1";
     3	import type * as schema from "../db/better-auth.ts";
     4	import { rewards, user as userTable } from "../db/better-auth.ts";
     5	import type { Bucket } from "./deduction.ts";
     6	import { POLLEN_BILLING_PRECISION } from "./precision.ts";
     7	
     8	export const MAX_REWARD_AMOUNT = 10_000;
     9	
    10	/**
    11	 * Idempotency key for a reward one person can earn once. Keyed on the GitHub
    12	 * id, else the Google account id. Both outlive the account row, so a
    13	 * deleted-and-recreated account cannot earn it again.
    14	 */
    15	export function rewardKey(
    16	    questId: string,
    17	    identity: { githubId?: number | null; googleId?: string | null },
    18	): string {
    19	    if (identity.githubId != null) {
    20	        return `quest:${questId}:github:${identity.githubId}`;
    21	    }
    22	    if (identity.googleId)
    23	        return `quest:${questId}:google:${identity.googleId}`;
    24	    throw new Error(`Reward ${questId} requires a GitHub or Google identity`);
    25	}
    26	
    27	export interface RecordRewardInput {
    28	    /**
    29	     * Idempotency guard. Must be deterministic for the logical reward so retries
    30	     * never create duplicates; encodes the quest's completion scope, e.g.
    31	     * "quest:{issue}" or rewardKey().
    32	     */
    33	    idempotencyKey: string;
    34	    userId: string;
    35	    amount: number;
    36	    /** Which balance bucket to credit on claim. */
    37	    bucket: Bucket;
    38	    /** Catalog id of the quest that was earned; null for one-off rewards. */
    39	    questId?: string | null;
    40	    /** Quest title, snapshotted so history renders it without a catalog lookup. */
    41	    title: string;
    42	    /** Optional quest link, snapshotted so history renders it directly. */
    43	    url?: string | null;
    44	}
    45	
    46	export interface RecordRewardsResult {
    47	    /** Number of newly created pending rewards. */
    48	    recorded: number;
    49	    /** IDs of newly created pending rewards. Duplicate inputs are omitted. */
    50	    rewardIds: string[];
    51	}
    52	
    53	export interface ClaimRewardResult {
    54	    claimed: boolean;
    55	    reward: {
    56	        id: string;
    57	        questId: string | null;
    58	        title: string;
    59	        pollenAmount: number;
    60	        balanceBucket: Bucket;
    61	        earnedAt: Date;
    62	        claimedAt: Date | null;
    63	    } | null;
    64	    newBalance: number | null;
    65	}
    66	
    67	type AuthDb = DrizzleD1Database<typeof schema>;
    68	
    69	function assertRewardAmount(amount: number): void {
    70	    if (!Number.isFinite(amount) || amount <= 0 || amount > MAX_REWARD_AMOUNT) {
    71	        throw new Error(
    72	            `reward amount must be > 0 and <= ${MAX_REWARD_AMOUNT}, got: ${amount}`,
    73	        );
    74	    }
    75	}
    76	
    77	/**
    78	 * Records earned rewards without moving pollen. The unique idempotency key
    79	 * makes scanner retries safe; only claimReward() credits the user's balance.
    80	 */
    81	export async function recordRewards(
    82	    db: AuthDb,
    83	    inputs: RecordRewardInput[],
    84	): Promise<RecordRewardsResult> {
    85	    if (inputs.length === 0) return { recorded: 0, rewardIds: [] };
    86	
    87	    const rows = inputs.map((input) => {
    88	        assertRewardAmount(input.amount);
    89	        return {
    90	            id: crypto.randomUUID(),
    91	            idempotencyKey: input.idempotencyKey,
    92	            userId: input.userId,
    93	            questId: input.questId ?? null,
    94	            title: input.title,
    95	            url: input.url ?? null,
    96	            pollenAmount: input.amount,
    97	            balanceBucket: input.bucket,
    98	            // Set earnedAt explicitly so drizzle stores it as Unix seconds
    99	            // (mode:"timestamp"), matching claimedAt and every other timestamp
   100	            // column. Relying on the column default emits milliseconds instead.
   101	            earnedAt: new Date(),
   102	        };
   103	    });
   104	
   105	    // Keep each insert as a separate statement so its bound parameter count is
   106	    // independent of the number of rewards. D1 executes the statements in one
   107	    // transactional batch, avoiding extra database round trips.
   108	    const statements = rows.map((row) =>
   109	        db
   110	            .insert(rewards)
   111	            .values(row)
   112	            .onConflictDoNothing({ target: rewards.idempotencyKey }),
   113	    );
   114	    const [firstStatement, ...remainingStatements] = statements;
   115	    if (!firstStatement) return { recorded: 0, rewardIds: [] };
   116	
   117	    const results = await db.batch([firstStatement, ...remainingStatements]);
   118	    const rewardIds = rows.flatMap((row, index) => {
   119	        const result = results[index] as D1Result | undefined;
   120	        return result?.meta.changes ? [row.id] : [];
   121	    });
   122	
   123	    return {
   124	        recorded: rewardIds.length,
   125	        rewardIds,
   126	    };
   127	}
   128	
   129	/**
   130	 * Claims one pending reward and credits the chosen balance bucket. The balance
   131	 * update is gated on the preceding `claimed_at IS NULL` update, so retries and
   132	 * double-clicks cannot double-pay. Account restrictions freeze spending, not claims.
   133	 */
   134	export async function claimReward(
   135	    db: AuthDb,
   136	    {
   137	        rewardId,
   138	        userId,
   139	    }: {
   140	        rewardId: string;
   141	        userId: string;
   142	    },
   143	): Promise<ClaimRewardResult> {
   144	    const row = await loadRewardForUser(db, rewardId, userId);
   145	    if (!row) return { claimed: false, reward: null, newBalance: null };
   146	    if (row.claimedAt !== null) {
   147	        return { claimed: false, reward: row, newBalance: null };
   148	    }
   149	
   150	    assertRewardAmount(row.pollenAmount);
   151	
   152	    const bucketColumn =
   153	        row.balanceBucket === "tier" ? sql`tier_balance` : sql`pack_balance`;
   154	    const claimedAt = new Date();
   155	
   156	    const [, updateResult] = await db.batch([
   157	        db
   158	            .update(rewards)
   159	            .set({ claimedAt })
   160	            .where(
   161	                and(
   162	                    eq(rewards.id, rewardId),
   163	                    eq(rewards.userId, userId),
   164	                    isNull(rewards.claimedAt),
   165	                ),
   166	            ),
   167	        db
   168	            .update(userTable)
   169	            .set({
   170	                [`${row.balanceBucket}Balance`]: sql`ROUND(COALESCE(${bucketColumn}, 0) + ${row.pollenAmount}, ${POLLEN_BILLING_PRECISION})`,
   171	            })
   172	            .where(sql`${userTable.id} = ${userId} AND changes() = 1`)
   173	            .returning({ newBalance: bucketColumn }),
   174	    ]);
   175	
   176	    const updatedRows =
   177	        (updateResult as Array<{ newBalance: number | null }>) ?? [];
   178	    const claimed = updatedRows.length === 1;
   179	    if (!claimed) {
   180	        const latest = await loadRewardForUser(db, rewardId, userId);
   181	        return { claimed: false, reward: latest, newBalance: null };
   182	    }
   183	
   184	    return {
   185	        claimed: true,
   186	        reward: { ...row, claimedAt },
   187	        newBalance: updatedRows[0]?.newBalance ?? null,
   188	    };
   189	}
   190	
   191	async function loadRewardForUser(
   192	    db: AuthDb,
   193	    rewardId: string,
   194	    userId: string,
   195	): Promise<ClaimRewardResult["reward"]> {
   196	    const rows = await db
   197	        .select({
   198	            id: rewards.id,
   199	            questId: rewards.questId,
   200	            title: rewards.title,
   201	            pollenAmount: rewards.pollenAmount,
   202	            balanceBucket: rewards.balanceBucket,
   203	            earnedAt: rewards.earnedAt,
   204	            claimedAt: rewards.claimedAt,
   205	        })
   206	        .from(rewards)
   207	        .where(and(eq(rewards.id, rewardId), eq(rewards.userId, userId)))
   208	        .limit(1);
   209	
   210	    const row = rows[0];
   211	    if (!row) return null;
   212	    return {
   213	        ...row,
   214	        balanceBucket: row.balanceBucket as Bucket,
   215	    };
   216	}
