    37	export type UpstreamHeaders = Record<string, string>;
    38	
    39	type UpstreamErrorOptions = {
    40	    res?: Response;
    41	    message?: string;
    42	    cause?: unknown;
    43	    requestUrl?: URL;
    44	    requestBody?: unknown;
    45	    upstreamStatus?: number;
    46	    responseBody?: string;
    47	    upstreamHeaders?: UpstreamHeaders;
    48	    /**
    49	     * Overrides the status-derived error code in the response envelope. Used to
    50	     * surface a stable, machine-readable code (e.g. `content_policy_violation`)
    51	     * that callers can detect regardless of the HTTP status.
    52	     */
    53	    errorCode?: OverrideErrorCode;
    54	    /**
    55	     * Usage the provider billed even though the request failed, such as an
    56	     * xAI video rejected after generation. Tracking charges it.
    57	     */
    58	    billedUsage?: Usage;
    59	};
    60	
    61	/** Public HTTP failure plus original provider diagnostics. Bodies are not redacted or truncated. */
    62	export class UpstreamError extends HTTPException {
    63	    public override readonly name: string = "UpstreamError";
    64	    public readonly requestUrl?: URL;
    65	    public readonly requestBody?: unknown;
    66	    public readonly upstreamStatus?: number;
    67	    public readonly responseBody?: string;
    68	    public readonly upstreamHeaders?: UpstreamHeaders;
    69	    public readonly errorCode?: OverrideErrorCode;
    70	    public readonly billedUsage?: Usage;
    71	
    72	    constructor(status: ContentfulStatusCode, options?: UpstreamErrorOptions) {
    73	        super(status, options);
    74	        this.requestUrl = options?.requestUrl;
    75	        this.requestBody = options?.requestBody;
    76	        this.upstreamStatus = options?.upstreamStatus;
    77	        this.responseBody = options?.responseBody;
    78	        this.upstreamHeaders = options?.upstreamHeaders;
    79	        this.errorCode = options?.errorCode;
    80	        this.billedUsage = options?.billedUsage;
    81	    }
    82	
    83	    /** Keep the provider status for diagnostics and retries; expose gateway failures as 5xx. */
    84	    static fromProvider(status: number, options: UpstreamErrorOptions) {
    85	        return new UpstreamError(remapUpstreamStatus(status), {
    86	            ...options,
    87	            upstreamStatus: status,
    88	        });
    89	    }
    90	}
    91	
    92	const REDACTED_HEADER_VALUE = "[redacted]";
    93	const SENSITIVE_HEADER_NAME =
    94	    /(^|[-_])(authorization|cookie|api[-_]?key|token|secret)([-_]|$)/i;
    95	
    96	/** Preserves upstream response headers while redacting credential-bearing values. */
    97	export function collectUpstreamHeaders(
    98	    headers: Headers,
    99	): UpstreamHeaders | undefined {
   100	    const entries = Array.from(headers.entries(), ([name, value]) => [
   101	        name,
   102	        SENSITIVE_HEADER_NAME.test(name) ? REDACTED_HEADER_VALUE : value,
   103	    ]);
   104	
   105	    return entries.length > 0 ? Object.fromEntries(entries) : undefined;
   106	}
   107	
   108	export async function ensureUpstreamOk(
   109	    response: Response,
   110	    requestUrl: string | URL,
   111	): Promise<Response> {
   112	    if (response.ok) return response;
   113	    let responseBody: string | undefined;
   114	    let cause: unknown;
   115	    try {
   116	        responseBody = await response.text();
   117	    } catch (error) {
   118	        cause = error;
   119	    }
   120	    const rawMessage =
   121	        (responseBody && extractUpstreamMessage(responseBody)) ||
   122	        (cause instanceof Error
   123	            ? cause.message
   124	            : getDefaultErrorMessage(response.status));
   125	    throw UpstreamError.fromProvider(response.status, {
   126	        message: rawMessage,
   127	        requestUrl:
   128	            typeof requestUrl === "string" ? new URL(requestUrl) : requestUrl,
   129	        responseBody,
   130	        cause,
   131	        upstreamHeaders: collectUpstreamHeaders(response.headers),
   132	    });
   133	}
   134	
   135	function extractUpstreamMessage(body: string): string {
   136	    try {
   137	        const parsed = JSON.parse(body);
   138	        const extracted =
   139	            parsed?.details?.error?.message ||
   140	            parsed?.error?.message ||
   141	            parsed?.message ||
   142	            (typeof parsed?.error === "string" ? parsed.error : null);
   143	        if (typeof extracted === "string" && extracted) return extracted;
   144	    } catch {
   145	        // Not JSON — fall through to raw body
   146	    }
   147	    return body;
   148	}
   149	
   150	/**
   151	 * Stable, machine-readable codes for failures involving a user-supplied image
   152	 * (URL or upload). Values are OpenAI `ResponseErrorCode` names so callers can
   153	 * branch on a code instead of parsing our error prose. All are returned with
   154	 * HTTP 400 — a bad user-supplied image is a client error, never an upstream one.
   155	 */
   156	export type ImageInputErrorCode =
   157	    | "failed_to_download_image"
   158	    | "invalid_image_url"
   159	    | "image_too_large"
   160	    | "unsupported_image_media_type";
   161	
   162	/**
   163	 * Codes we emit in place of the status-derived code, keyed by the status they
   164	 * are emitted with. The response envelope's `code` is therefore not always
   165	 * `getErrorCode(status)`, and the published schema must say so. `errorCode`
   166	 * is typed from this map, so a code missing here fails the typecheck.
   167	 */
   168	const OVERRIDE_ERROR_CODES = {
   169	    402: [
   170	        "KEY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED",
   171	        "INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE",
   172	        "QUEST_POLLEN_RESTRICTED",
   173	        "QUEST_POLLEN_ONLY",
   174	    ],
   175	    400: [
   176	        "content_blocked",
   177	        // Vertex, Vercel Google and xAI video moderation; the rest use 422.
   178	        "content_policy_violation",
   179	        "failed_to_download_image",
   180	        "invalid_image_url",
   181	        "image_too_large",
   182	        "unsupported_image_media_type",
   183	        "output_token_limit_exceeded",
   184	        "unsupported_parameter",
   185	    ],
   186	    422: ["content_policy_violation"],
   187	    429: ["community_model_rate_limit"],
   188	    502: ["empty_response"],
   189	} as const;
   190	
   191	export type OverrideErrorCode =
   192	    (typeof OVERRIDE_ERROR_CODES)[keyof typeof OVERRIDE_ERROR_CODES][number];
   193	
   194	export function getErrorCodesForStatus(status: number): [string, ...string[]] {
   195	    const overrides: Record<number, readonly string[]> = OVERRIDE_ERROR_CODES;
   196	    return [getErrorCode(status), ...(overrides[status] ?? [])];
   197	}
   198	
   199	const GenericErrorDetailsSchema = z
   200	    .object({
   201	        name: z.string(),
   202	        upstreamStatus: z.number().int().optional(),
   203	        upstreamHost: z.string().optional(),
   204	        upstreamBody: z
   205	            .string()
   206	            .describe(
   207	                "Original provider response body, without redaction or truncation.",
   208	            )
   209	            .optional(),
   210	    })
   211	    .meta({ $id: "ErrorDetails" });
   212	
   213	const ValidationErrorDetailsSchema = z
   214	    .object({
   215	        name: z.string(),
   216	        formErrors: z.array(z.string()),
   217	        fieldErrors: z.record(z.string(), z.array(z.string())),
   218	    })
   219	    .meta({ $id: "ValidationErrorDetails" });
   220	
   221	const FixUrlSchema = z
   222	    .string()
   223	    .describe(
   224	        "Page where the API key's owner can fix this error, such as allowing a model, raising the key budget or topping up.",
   225	    )
   226	    .optional();
   227	
   228	export function createErrorResponseSchema(
   229	    status: ContentfulStatusCode,
   230	): z.ZodObject {
   231	    // An upstream input error keeps its 400 status but carries upstream details,
   232	    // so a 400 has two possible shapes.
   233	    const errorDetailsSchema =
   234	        status === 400
   235	            ? z.union([ValidationErrorDetailsSchema, GenericErrorDetailsSchema])
   236	            : GenericErrorDetailsSchema;
   237	    return z.object({
   238	        status: z.literal(status),
   239	        success: z.literal(false),
   240	        error: z.object({
   241	            code: z.enum(getErrorCodesForStatus(status)),
   242	            message: z.union([
   243	                z.literal(getDefaultErrorMessage(status)),
   244	                z.string(),
   245	            ]),
   246	            timestamp: z.string(),
   247	            // Only sent when there are details, e.g. validation or upstream errors.
   248	            details: errorDetailsSchema.optional(),
   249	            requestId: z.string().optional(),
   250	            fixUrl: FixUrlSchema,
   251	        }),
   252	    });
   253	}
   254	
   255	export const GenericErrorResponseSchema = z.object({
   256	    status: z.number().int().min(100).max(599),
   257	    success: z.boolean(),
   258	    error: z.object({
   259	        code: z.string(),
   260	        message: z.string(),
   261	        timestamp: z.string(),
   262	        details: GenericErrorDetailsSchema.optional(),
   263	        requestId: z.string().optional(),
   264	        fixUrl: FixUrlSchema,
   265	    }),
   266	});
   267	
   268	const ErrorResponseSchema = z.discriminatedUnion("status", [
   269	    createErrorResponseSchema(400),
   270	    GenericErrorResponseSchema,
   271	]);
   272	
   273	type ErrorResponse = z.infer<typeof ErrorResponseSchema>;
   274	
   275	type ServerErrorEnvelope = {
   276	    kind: "server_error";
   277	    severity: "error";
   278	    timestamp: string;
   279	    requestId?: string;
   280	    environment?: string;
   281	    routePath: string;
   282	    method: string;
   283	    status: number;
   284	    durationMs?: number;
   285	    errorCode: string;
   286	    errorClass: string;
   287	    message: string;
   288	    stack?: string;
   289	    upstreamHost?: string;
   290	    upstreamStatus?: number;
   291	    upstreamBody?: string;
   292	    edgeColo?: string;
   293	    upstreamHeaders?: UpstreamHeaders;
   294	    modelRequested?: string;
   295	    resolvedModelRequested?: string;
   296	    requestInputs?: RequestInputs;
   297	    userId?: string;
   298	    userTier?: string;
   299	    apiKeyId?: string;
   300	};
   301	
   302	const MAX_ERROR_MESSAGE_LENGTH = 2000;
   303	const MAX_STACK_LENGTH = 12000;
   304	const MAX_UPSTREAM_BODY_LENGTH = 16000;
   305	
   306	// Drizzle/D1 errors embed the failing SQL text and its bound parameters, which
   307	// include stored API key hashes. They belong in the logs, never in a response.
   308	const QUERY_ERROR_PATTERN = /Failed query:|\nparams: /;
   309	
   310	export async function handleError<TEnv extends ErrorHandlerEnv>(
   311	    err: Error,
   312	    c: Context<TEnv>,
   313	) {
   314	    // Use getLogger directly instead of c.get("log"). The error handler must
   315	    // never depend on logger middleware having run successfully — getLogger is
   316	    // idempotent (returns the same singleton for the same category).
   317	    const log = getLogger(["hono"]);
   318	    const timestamp = new Date().toISOString();
   319	
   320	    // Set the error on the context for it to be tracked
   321	    c.set("error", err);
   322	
   323	    if (err instanceof UpstreamError) {
   324	        const status = err.status;
   325	        if (status >= 500)
   326	            await emitServerError(c, err, status, timestamp, log);
   327	        else {
   328	            log.trace("UpstreamError: {message}", {
   329	                message: err.message || getDefaultErrorMessage(err.status),
   330	            });
   331	        }
   332	        return c.json(
   333	            createUpstreamErrorResponse(err, status, timestamp),
   334	            status,
   335	        );
   336	    }
   337	
   338	    if (err instanceof HTTPException) {
   339	        const status = err.status;
   340	        if (status >= 500)
   341	            await emitServerError(c, err, status, timestamp, log);
   342	        else {
   343	            log.trace("HttpException: {message}", {
   344	                message: err.message || getDefaultErrorMessage(err.status),
   345	            });
   346	        }
   347	        return c.json(
   348	            createErrorResponse(err, status, timestamp, {
   349	                code:
   350	                    err instanceof PaymentRequiredError
   351	                        ? err.errorCode
   352	                        : undefined,
   353	                fixUrl:
   354	                    err instanceof PaymentRequiredError ||
   355	                    err instanceof PermissionRequiredError
   356	                        ? err.fixUrl
   357	                        : undefined,
   358	            }),
   359	            status,
   360	        );
   361	    }
   362	
   363	    if (err instanceof APIError) {
   364	        const status = err.statusCode as ContentfulStatusCode;
   365	        if (status >= 500)
   366	            await emitServerError(c, err, status, timestamp, log);
   367	        else log.trace("APIError: {error}", { error: err });
   368	        return c.json(createErrorResponse(err, status, timestamp), status);
   369	    }
   370	
   371	    if (err instanceof ValidationError) {
   372	        const status = 400;
   373	        const response = createValidationErrorResponse(err, status, timestamp);
   374	        log.trace("ValidationError: {error}", { error: err });
   375	        return c.json(response, status);
   376	    }
   377	
   378	    const status = 500;
   379	    await emitServerError(c, err, status, timestamp, log);
   380	    const response = createInternalErrorResponse(err, status, timestamp);
   381	    return c.json(response, status);
   382	}
   383	
   384	/**
   385	 * Creates a standardized error response
   386	 */
   387	function createErrorResponse(
   388	    error: Error,
   389	    status: ContentfulStatusCode,
   390	    timestamp: string,
   391	    {
   392	        details,
   393	        code,
   394	        fixUrl,
   395	        message,
   396	    }: {
   397	        details?: Record<string, unknown>;
   398	        code?: OverrideErrorCode;
   399	        fixUrl?: string;
   400	        message?: string;
   401	    } = {},
   402	): ErrorResponse {
   403	    return {
   404	        success: false,
   405	        error: {
   406	            message: message ?? publicErrorMessage(error, status),
   407	            code: code ?? getErrorCode(status),
   408	            timestamp,
   409	            ...(details && { details }),
   410	            ...(fixUrl && { fixUrl }),
   411	        },
   412	        status,
   413	    };
   414	}
   415	
   416	/**
   417	 * A 5xx body may carry the error message, but a database failure describes the
   418	 * query and its bound parameters. `emitServerError` has already logged the full
   419	 * error, so answer with the generic message instead of leaking the SQL text and
   420	 * stored API key hashes.
   421	 */
   422	function publicErrorMessage(
   423	    error: Error,
   424	    status: ContentfulStatusCode,
   425	): string {
   426	    const message = error.message || getDefaultErrorMessage(status);
   427	    return status >= 500 && QUERY_ERROR_PATTERN.test(message)
   428	        ? getDefaultErrorMessage(status)
   429	        : message;
   430	}
   431	
   432	function createValidationErrorResponse(
   433	    error: ValidationError,
   434	    status: ContentfulStatusCode,
   435	    timestamp: string,
   436	): ErrorResponse {
   437	    const flatErrors = z.flattenError(error.zodError);
   438	    return createErrorResponse(error, status, timestamp, {
   439	        details: { name: error.name, ...flatErrors },
   440	    });
   441	}
   442	
   443	// Unexpected errors can carry any internal detail, not only query dumps.
   444	// Callers get the default message; the server_error log keeps the error.
   445	function createInternalErrorResponse(
   446	    error: Error,
   447	    status: ContentfulStatusCode,
   448	    timestamp: string,
   449	): ErrorResponse {
   450	    return createErrorResponse(error, status, timestamp, {
   451	        details: { name: error.name },
   452	        message: getDefaultErrorMessage(status),
   453	    });
   454	}
   455	
   456	function createUpstreamErrorResponse(
   457	    error: UpstreamError,
   458	    status: ContentfulStatusCode,
   459	    timestamp: string,
   460	): ErrorResponse {
   461	    return createErrorResponse(error, status, timestamp, {
   462	        details: {
   463	            name: error.name,
   464	            upstreamStatus: error.upstreamStatus,
   465	            upstreamHost: error.requestUrl?.hostname,
   466	            upstreamBody: error.responseBody,
   467	        },
   468	        code: error.errorCode,
   469	    });
   470	}
   471	
   472	/**
   473	 * Remap upstream statuses that are our operational concern (auth, routing,
   474	 * quota, conflicts, proxy timeouts) to 502 Bad Gateway. Leaves input-content
   475	 * errors (400/413/415/422) as-is since those can reflect user input we failed to
   476	 * validate.
   477	 */
   478	export function remapUpstreamStatus(status: number): ContentfulStatusCode {
   479	    // A timeout waiting on our provider is a gateway failure, not a caller's
   480	    // incomplete request. Keep upstreamStatus separately for retry decisions.
   481	    if (status === 408) return 504;
   482	    const remapTo502 = new Set([401, 402, 403, 404, 409, 429, 524]);
   483	    if (remapTo502.has(status)) return 502;
   484	    return status as ContentfulStatusCode;
   485	}
   486	
   487	export function getErrorCode(status: number): string {
   488	    const codes: Record<number, string> = {
   489	        400: "BAD_REQUEST",
   490	        401: "UNAUTHORIZED",
   491	        402: "PAYMENT_REQUIRED",
   492	        403: "FORBIDDEN",
   493	        404: "NOT_FOUND",
   494	        405: "METHOD_NOT_ALLOWED",
   495	        408: "REQUEST_TIMEOUT",
   496	        409: "CONFLICT",
   497	        410: "GONE",
   498	        413: "PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE",
   499	        415: "UNSUPPORTED_MEDIA_TYPE",
   500	        422: "UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY",
   501	        426: "UPGRADE_REQUIRED",
   502	        429: "RATE_LIMITED",
   503	        500: "INTERNAL_ERROR",
   504	        502: "BAD_GATEWAY",
   505	        503: "SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE",
   506	        504: "GATEWAY_TIMEOUT",
   507	    };
   508	    return codes[status] || "UNKNOWN_ERROR";
   509	}

   511	export const KNOWN_ERROR_STATUS_CODES = [
   512	    400, 401, 402, 403, 404, 405, 408, 409, 410, 413, 415, 422, 426, 429, 500,
   513	    502, 503, 504,
   514	] as const;
   515	
   516	export type ErrorStatusCode = (typeof KNOWN_ERROR_STATUS_CODES)[number];

   518	export function getDefaultErrorMessage(status: number): string {
   519	    const messages: Record<number, string> = {
   520	        400: "Something was wrong with the input data, check the details for more info.",
   521	        401: "Authentication required. Please provide an API key via Authorization header (Bearer token) or ?key= query parameter.",
   522	        402: "Insufficient pollen balance or API key budget exhausted.",
   523	        403: "Access denied! You don't have the required permissions for this resource or model.",
   524	        404: "Oh no, there's nothing here.",
   525	        405: "That HTTP method isn't supported here. Please check the API docs.",
   526	        408: "The request was not received in time.",
   527	        409: "Something with these details already exists. Maybe update it instead?",
   528	        410: "This resource is no longer available.",
   529	        413: "The request payload is too large. Reduce its size and try again.",
   530	        415: "The request media type isn't supported.",
   531	        422: "Your request looks good, but some required fields are missing or invalid.",
   532	        426: "This endpoint requires a WebSocket upgrade request.",
   533	        429: "You're making requests too quickly. Please slow down a bit.",
   534	        500: "Oh snap, something went wrong on our end. We're on it!",
   535	        502: "We couldn't reach our backend services. Please try again shortly.",
   536	        503: "We're temporarily down for maintenance. Sorry about that!",
   537	        504: "The upstream service did not respond in time.",
   538	    };
   539	    return messages[status] || "UNKNOWN_ERROR";
   540	}

   542	/**
   543	 * Reports a 5xx that never reached `handleError`, such as one Better Auth
   544	 * answered itself. Its request inputs stay out: auth requests carry OAuth
   545	 * codes and client secrets.
   546	 */
   547	export async function reportServerError<TEnv extends ErrorHandlerEnv>(
   548	    c: Context<TEnv>,
   549	    error: Error,
   550	    status: number,
   551	): Promise<void> {
   552	    const timestamp = new Date().toISOString();
   553	    await emitServerError(c, error, status, timestamp, getLogger(["hono"]), {
   554	        withInputs: false,
   555	    });
   556	}
   557	
   558	async function emitServerError<TEnv extends ErrorHandlerEnv>(
   559	    c: Context<TEnv>,
   560	    error: Error,
   561	    status: number,
   562	    timestamp: string,
   563	    log: Logger,
   564	    { withInputs = true } = {},
   565	): Promise<void> {
   566	    const envelope = await createServerErrorEnvelope(
   567	        c,
   568	        error,
   569	        status,
   570	        timestamp,
   571	        withInputs,
   572	    );
   573	    log.error(
   574	        "server_error route={routePath} status={status} class={errorClass}",
   575	        envelope,
   576	    );
   577	
   578	    c.executionCtx.waitUntil(
   579	        sendErrorEventToTinybird(
   580	            toTinybirdErrorEvent(envelope),
   581	            getTinybirdDatasourceIngestUrl(
   582	                c.env.TINYBIRD_INGEST_URL,
   583	                "error_event",
   584	            ),
   585	            c.env.TINYBIRD_INGEST_TOKEN,
   586	            log,
   587	        ),
   588	    );
   589	}
   590	
   591	async function createServerErrorEnvelope<TEnv extends ErrorHandlerEnv>(
   592	    c: Context<TEnv>,
   593	    error: Error,
   594	    status: number,
   595	    timestamp: string,
   596	    withInputs: boolean,
   597	): Promise<ServerErrorEnvelope> {
   598	    const vars = c.var as Partial<{
   599	        auth: {
   600	            user?: { id?: string; tier?: string };
   601	            apiKey?: { id?: string };
   602	        };
   603	        model: {
   604	            requested: string;
   605	            resolved: string;
   606	        };
   607	        requestStartedAt: number;
   608	    }>;
   609	    const message =
   610	        truncateString(
   611	            error.message || getDefaultErrorMessage(status),
   612	            MAX_ERROR_MESSAGE_LENGTH,
   613	        ) || getDefaultErrorMessage(status);
   614	    const stack = truncateString(stackWithCause(error), MAX_STACK_LENGTH);
   615	    const resolvedRoutePath = getRoutePath(c);
   616	    const edgeColo = (
   617	        c.req.raw as Request & {
   618	            cf?: { colo?: string };
   619	        }
   620	    ).cf?.colo;
   621	
   622	    return {
   623	        kind: "server_error",
   624	        severity: "error",
   625	        timestamp,
   626	        requestId: c.get("requestId"),
   627	        environment: c.env.ENVIRONMENT,
   628	        routePath: resolvedRoutePath,
   629	        method: c.req.method,
   630	        status,
   631	        durationMs:
   632	            vars.requestStartedAt === undefined
   633	                ? undefined
   634	                : Date.now() - vars.requestStartedAt,
   635	        errorCode: getErrorCode(status),
   636	        errorClass: error.name,
   637	        message,
   638	        stack,
   639	        upstreamHost:
   640	            error instanceof UpstreamError
   641	                ? error.requestUrl?.hostname
   642	                : undefined,
   643	        upstreamStatus:
   644	            error instanceof UpstreamError ? error.upstreamStatus : undefined,
   645	        upstreamBody:
   646	            error instanceof UpstreamError
   647	                ? truncateString(error.responseBody, MAX_UPSTREAM_BODY_LENGTH)
   648	                : undefined,
   649	        edgeColo,
   650	        upstreamHeaders:
   651	            error instanceof UpstreamError ? error.upstreamHeaders : undefined,
   652	        modelRequested: vars.model?.requested,
   653	        resolvedModelRequested: vars.model?.resolved,
   654	        requestInputs: withInputs ? await collectRequestInputs(c) : undefined,
   655	        userId: vars.auth?.user?.id,
   656	        userTier: vars.auth?.user?.tier,
   657	        apiKeyId: vars.auth?.apiKey?.id,
   658	    };
   659	}
   660	
   661	function stackWithCause(error: Error): string | undefined {
   662	    const cause = error.cause;
   663	    if (!(cause instanceof Error) && typeof cause !== "string") {
   664	        return error.stack;
   665	    }
   666	    const properties = cause as Error & Record<string, unknown>;
   667	    const flags = ["durableObjectReset", "overloaded", "retryable"]
   668	        .filter((key) => typeof properties[key] === "boolean")
   669	        .map((key) => `${key}=${properties[key]}`)
   670	        .join(" ");
   671	    const detail =
   672	        cause instanceof Error
   673	            ? cause.stack || `${cause.name}: ${cause.message}`
   674	            : cause;
   675	    // Put the underlying failure first so truncation keeps the useful detail.
   676	    // Do not serialize arbitrary error properties or traverse cause chains.
   677	    return `Caused by: ${flags}\n${detail}\nWrapped by: ${error.stack ?? error.message}`;
   678	}
   679	
   680	function toTinybirdErrorEvent(
   681	    envelope: ServerErrorEnvelope,
   682	): TinybirdErrorEvent {
   683	    return {
   684	        timestamp: envelope.timestamp,
   685	        kind: envelope.kind,
   686	        severity: envelope.severity,
   687	        request_id: envelope.requestId,
   688	        environment: envelope.environment,
   689	        route_path: envelope.routePath,
   690	        method: envelope.method,
   691	        status: envelope.status,
   692	        duration_ms: envelope.durationMs,
   693	        error_code: envelope.errorCode,
   694	        error_class: envelope.errorClass,
   695	        message: envelope.message,
   696	        stack: envelope.stack,
   697	        upstream_host: envelope.upstreamHost,
   698	        upstream_status: envelope.upstreamStatus,
   699	        upstream_body: envelope.upstreamBody,
   700	        edge_colo: envelope.edgeColo,
   701	        upstream_headers: envelope.upstreamHeaders
   702	            ? JSON.stringify(envelope.upstreamHeaders)
   703	            : undefined,
   704	        model_requested: envelope.modelRequested,
   705	        resolved_model_requested: envelope.resolvedModelRequested,
   706	        request_inputs: stringifyRequestInputs(envelope.requestInputs),
   707	        user_id: envelope.userId,
   708	        user_tier: envelope.userTier,
   709	        api_key_id: envelope.apiKeyId,
   710	    };
   711	}
   712	
   713	function truncateString(
   714	    value: string | undefined,
   715	    maxLength: number,
   716	): string | undefined {
   717	    if (!value) return undefined;
   718	    if (value.length <= maxLength) return value;
   719	    return `${value.slice(0, maxLength)}...`;
   720	}
===== shared/events.ts =====
     1	import type { Logger } from "@logtape/logtape";
     2	import type { TinybirdEvent } from "./schemas/generation-event.ts";
     3	import { removeUnset } from "./util.ts";
     4	
     5	export type TinybirdErrorEvent = {
     6	    timestamp: string;
     7	    kind: "server_error" | "d1_call";
     8	    severity: "error" | "warning";
     9	    request_id?: string;
    10	    environment?: string;
    11	    route_path?: string;
    12	    method?: string;
    13	    status: number;
    14	    duration_ms?: number;
    15	    error_code?: string;
    16	    error_class?: string;
    17	    message?: string;
    18	    stack?: string;
    19	    upstream_host?: string;
    20	    upstream_status?: number;
    21	    upstream_body?: string;
    22	    edge_colo?: string;
    23	    upstream_headers?: string;
    24	    model_requested?: string;
    25	    resolved_model_requested?: string;
    26	    request_inputs?: string;
    27	    user_id?: string;
    28	    user_tier?: string;
    29	    api_key_id?: string;
    30	};
    31	
    32	export async function sendToTinybird(
    33	    event: TinybirdEvent,
    34	    tinybirdIngestUrl: string,
    35	    tinybirdIngestToken: string,
    36	    log: Logger,
    37	): Promise<void> {
    38	    // Tinybird's historical image columns are UInt32. Fractional usage belongs
    39	    // in Float64 unit columns; never round it or send it to an integer column.
    40	    const body = JSON.stringify(
    41	        removeUnset({
    42	            ...event,
    43	            usagePromptImageUnits: event.tokenCountPromptImage,
    44	            usageCompletionImageUnits: event.tokenCountCompletionImage,
    45	            tokenCountPromptImage: Number.isInteger(event.tokenCountPromptImage)
    46	                ? event.tokenCountPromptImage
    47	                : undefined,
    48	            tokenCountCompletionImage: Number.isInteger(
    49	                event.tokenCountCompletionImage,
    50	            )
    51	                ? event.tokenCountCompletionImage
    52	                : undefined,
    53	        }),
    54	    );
    55	
    56	    try {
    57	        const response = await fetch(tinybirdIngestUrl, {
    58	            method: "POST",
    59	            headers: {
    60	                Authorization: `Bearer ${tinybirdIngestToken}`,
    61	                "Content-Type": "application/x-ndjson",
    62	            },
    63	            body,
    64	        });
    65	
    66	        if (!response.ok) {
    67	            log.error("Tinybird API error: status={status} error={error}", {
    68	                status: response.status,
    69	                error: await response.text(),
    70	            });
    71	        }
    72	    } catch (error) {
    73	        log.error("Failed to send event to Tinybird: {error}", { error });
    74	    }
    75	}
    76	
    77	export async function sendErrorEventToTinybird(
    78	    event: TinybirdErrorEvent,
    79	    tinybirdIngestUrl: string,
    80	    tinybirdIngestToken: string,
    81	    log: Logger,
    82	): Promise<void> {
    83	    const body = JSON.stringify(removeUnset(event));
    84	
    85	    try {
    86	        const response = await fetch(tinybirdIngestUrl, {
    87	            method: "POST",
    88	            headers: {
    89	                Authorization: `Bearer ${tinybirdIngestToken}`,
    90	                "Content-Type": "application/x-ndjson",
    91	            },
    92	            body,
    93	            signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000),
    94	        });
    95	
    96	        if (!response.ok) {
    97	            log.warn("Tinybird error event ingest failed: status={status}", {
    98	                status: response.status,
    99	            });
   100	        }
   101	    } catch (error) {
   102	        log.warn("Tinybird error event ingest failed: {error}", { error });
   103	    }
   104	}
   105	
   106	export function getTinybirdDatasourceIngestUrl(
   107	    referenceIngestUrl: string,
   108	    datasourceName: string,
   109	): string {
   110	    const url = new URL(referenceIngestUrl);
   111	    url.searchParams.set("name", datasourceName);
   112	    return url.toString();
   113	}
===== shared/github/app-auth.ts =====
     1	/**
     2	 * GitHub App authentication for Cloudflare Workers — mints a short-lived
     3	 * installation access token using ONLY WebCrypto (`crypto.subtle`), the crypto
     4	 * surface available in a Worker. No Node `crypto`, no `jsonwebtoken`.
     5	 *
     6	 * Flow: RS256-sign a JWT with the App private key -> exchange it at
     7	 * POST /app/installations/{id}/access_tokens -> get a ~1h installation token.
     8	 *
     9	 * The App private key downloaded from GitHub is PKCS#1 ("BEGIN RSA PRIVATE
    10	 * KEY"), but `crypto.subtle.importKey('pkcs8', ...)` only accepts PKCS#8. So we
    11	 * wrap PKCS#1 -> PKCS#8 in pure JS (`pkcs1ToPkcs8`) before importing. This is
    12	 * the one non-obvious bit; everything else is a standard JWT.
    13	 */
    14	
    15	const GITHUB_API = "https://api.github.com";
    16	const USER_AGENT = "pollinations-enter";
    17	
    18	export type GithubAppCredentials = {
    19	    appId: string;
    20	    /** PEM private key. May be PKCS#1 or PKCS#8; \n may be escaped as "\\n". */
    21	    privateKey: string;
    22	};
    23	
    24	type CachedToken = {
    25	    token: string;
    26	    /** epoch ms when the token expires (per GitHub's `expires_at`). */
    27	    expiresAtMs: number;
    28	    /** the installation id this token was minted for. */
    29	    installationId: number;
    30	};
    31	
    32	// Module-scoped cache. Installation tokens last ~1h; we reuse one until it is
    33	// within REFRESH_SKEW_MS of expiry. In a Worker this cache lives for the
    34	// isolate's lifetime — good enough to avoid minting a token on every cron tick.
    35	let cached: CachedToken | null = null;
    36	let cachedInstallationId: number | null = null;
    37	const REFRESH_SKEW_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000; // refresh 5 min before expiry
    38	
    39	// ---- base64url helpers (Worker-safe: atob/btoa are global) ----
    40	
    41	function b64urlFromBytes(bytes: Uint8Array): string {
    42	    let bin = "";
    43	    for (const b of bytes) bin += String.fromCharCode(b);
    44	    return btoa(bin).replace(/\+/g, "-").replace(/\//g, "_").replace(/=+$/, "");
    45	}
    46	
    47	function b64urlFromString(str: string): string {
    48	    return b64urlFromBytes(new TextEncoder().encode(str));
    49	}
    50	
    51	function bytesFromB64(b64: string): Uint8Array {
    52	    const bin = atob(b64);
    53	    const out = new Uint8Array(bin.length);
    54	    for (let i = 0; i < bin.length; i++) out[i] = bin.charCodeAt(i);
    55	    return out;
    56	}
    57	
    58	// ---- PEM -> DER ----
    59	
    60	function pemToDer(pem: string): Uint8Array {
    61	    const body = pem
    62	        .replace(/-----BEGIN [A-Z ]+-----/, "")
    63	        .replace(/-----END [A-Z ]+-----/, "")
    64	        .replace(/\s+/g, "");
    65	    return bytesFromB64(body);
    66	}
    67	
    68	// ---- minimal DER encoding for the PKCS#1 -> PKCS#8 wrap ----
    69	
    70	function derLength(n: number): number[] {
    71	    if (n < 0x80) return [n];
    72	    const bytes: number[] = [];
    73	    let v = n;
    74	    while (v > 0) {
    75	        bytes.unshift(v & 0xff);
    76	        v >>= 8;
    77	    }
    78	    return [0x80 | bytes.length, ...bytes];
    79	}
    80	
    81	function derTLV(tag: number, content: Uint8Array): Uint8Array {
    82	    return Uint8Array.from([tag, ...derLength(content.length), ...content]);
    83	}
    84	
    85	function concatBytes(...arrs: Uint8Array[]): Uint8Array {
    86	    const total = arrs.reduce((s, a) => s + a.length, 0);
    87	    const out = new Uint8Array(total);
    88	    let off = 0;
    89	    for (const a of arrs) {
    90	        out.set(a, off);
    91	        off += a.length;
    92	    }
    93	    return out;
    94	}
    95	
    96	/**
    97	 * Wrap a PKCS#1 RSAPrivateKey DER into a PKCS#8 PrivateKeyInfo DER so WebCrypto
    98	 * can import it. PKCS#8 = SEQUENCE { INTEGER 0, AlgorithmIdentifier(rsaEncryption
    99	 * + NULL), OCTET STRING (the PKCS#1 DER) }.
   100	 */
   101	function pkcs1ToPkcs8(pkcs1Der: Uint8Array): Uint8Array {
   102	    const version = derTLV(0x02, Uint8Array.from([0x00]));
   103	    const rsaOid = derTLV(
   104	        0x06,
   105	        Uint8Array.from([0x2a, 0x86, 0x48, 0x86, 0xf7, 0x0d, 0x01, 0x01, 0x01]),
   106	    );
   107	    const nullParam = derTLV(0x05, Uint8Array.from([]));
   108	    const algId = derTLV(0x30, concatBytes(rsaOid, nullParam));
   109	    const privOctet = derTLV(0x04, pkcs1Der);
   110	    return derTLV(0x30, concatBytes(version, algId, privOctet));
   111	}
   112	
   113	function normalizePem(privateKey: string): string {
   114	    let pem = privateKey;
   115	    // SOPS dotenv stores the multi-line PEM with literal \n escapes.
   116	    if (pem.includes("\\n")) pem = pem.replace(/\\n/g, "\n");
   117	    // strip accidental surrounding quotes
   118	    return pem.replace(/^["']/, "").replace(/["']$/, "");
   119	}
   120	
   121	async function importSigningKey(privateKey: string): Promise<CryptoKey> {
   122	    const pem = normalizePem(privateKey);
   123	    const der = pemToDer(pem);
   124	    const pkcs8 = /BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY/.test(pem) ? pkcs1ToPkcs8(der) : der;
   125	    return crypto.subtle.importKey(
   126	        "pkcs8",
   127	        pkcs8 as BufferSource,
   128	        { name: "RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5", hash: "SHA-256" },
   129	        false,
   130	        ["sign"],
   131	    );
   132	}
   133	
   134	/** Mint a short-lived App JWT (valid ~9 min, iat backdated for clock skew). */
   135	async function mintAppJwt(creds: GithubAppCredentials): Promise<string> {
   136	    const key = await importSigningKey(creds.privateKey);
   137	    const nowSec = Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000);
   138	    const header = { alg: "RS256", typ: "JWT" };
   139	    const payload = { iat: nowSec - 60, exp: nowSec + 540, iss: creds.appId };
   140	    const signingInput = `${b64urlFromString(JSON.stringify(header))}.${b64urlFromString(
   141	        JSON.stringify(payload),
   142	    )}`;
   143	    const sig = await crypto.subtle.sign(
   144	        "RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5",
   145	        key,
   146	        new TextEncoder().encode(signingInput),
   147	    );
   148	    return `${signingInput}.${b64urlFromBytes(new Uint8Array(sig))}`;
   149	}
   150	
   151	async function appJsonGet<T>(path: string, jwt: string): Promise<T> {
   152	    const res = await fetch(`${GITHUB_API}${path}`, {
   153	        headers: {
   154	            Authorization: `Bearer ${jwt}`,
   155	            Accept: "application/vnd.github+json",
   156	            "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2022-11-28",
   157	            "User-Agent": USER_AGENT,
   158	        },
   159	    });
   160	    if (!res.ok) {
   161	        throw new Error(
   162	            `GitHub App GET ${path} -> ${res.status}: ${await res.text()}`,
   163	        );
   164	    }
   165	    return (await res.json()) as T;
   166	}
   167	
   168	/**
   169	 * Resolve the installation id for the given org account (cached). We match by
   170	 * `account.login` rather than taking the first installation, so this stays
   171	 * correct if the App ever gains a second installation. (The repo-scoped
   172	 * `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/installation` endpoint 404s for this App, so we
   173	 * list installations and pick the org's.)
   174	 */
   175	async function resolveInstallationId(
   176	    jwt: string,
   177	    org: string,
   178	): Promise<number> {
   179	    if (cachedInstallationId !== null) return cachedInstallationId;
   180	    const installations = await appJsonGet<
   181	        Array<{ id: number; account: { login: string } | null }>
   182	    >("/app/installations", jwt);
   183	    const match = installations.find(
   184	        (i) => i.account?.login?.toLowerCase() === org.toLowerCase(),
   185	    );
   186	    if (!match) {
   187	        throw new Error(
   188	            `GitHub App has no installation for org "${org}" (found: ${
   189	                installations.map((i) => i.account?.login).join(", ") || "none"
   190	            })`,
   191	        );
   192	    }
   193	    cachedInstallationId = match.id;
   194	    return cachedInstallationId;
   195	}
   196	
   197	/**
   198	 * Get a valid installation access token, minting (and caching) a new one only
   199	 * when none is cached or the cached one is near expiry. The returned token is
   200	 * used as `Authorization: token <token>` against the REST and GraphQL APIs.
   201	 */
   202	export async function getInstallationToken(
   203	    creds: GithubAppCredentials,
   204	    org: string,
   205	): Promise<string> {
   206	    if (cached && cached.expiresAtMs - Date.now() > REFRESH_SKEW_MS) {
   207	        return cached.token;
   208	    }
   209	
   210	    const jwt = await mintAppJwt(creds);
   211	    const installationId = await resolveInstallationId(jwt, org);
   212	
   213	    const res = await fetch(
   214	        `${GITHUB_API}/app/installations/${installationId}/access_tokens`,
   215	        {
   216	            method: "POST",
   217	            headers: {
   218	                Authorization: `Bearer ${jwt}`,
   219	                Accept: "application/vnd.github+json",
   220	                "X-GitHub-Api-Version": "2022-11-28",
   221	                "User-Agent": USER_AGENT,
   222	            },
   223	        },
   224	    );
   225	    if (res.status !== 201) {
   226	        throw new Error(
   227	            `GitHub installation token mint -> ${res.status}: ${await res.text()}`,
   228	        );
   229	    }
   230	    const body = (await res.json()) as { token: string; expires_at: string };
   231	    cached = {
   232	        token: body.token,
   233	        expiresAtMs: new Date(body.expires_at).getTime(),
   234	        installationId,
   235	    };
   236	    return cached.token;
   237	}
   238	
   239	/** Read App credentials off a Worker env. Throws if either is missing. */
   240	export function githubAppCredentialsFromEnv(env: {
   241	    GITHUB_APP_ID?: string;
   242	    GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY?: string;
   243	}): GithubAppCredentials {
   244	    if (!env.GITHUB_APP_ID || !env.GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY) {
   245	        throw new Error(
   246	            "missing GITHUB_APP_ID or GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY in env",
   247	        );
   248	    }
   249	    return { appId: env.GITHUB_APP_ID, privateKey: env.GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY };
   250	}

===== shared/github/client.ts =====
     1	/** Minimal GitHub GraphQL client for GitHub App installation tokens. */
     2	
     3	const GITHUB_API = "https://api.github.com";
     4	const USER_AGENT = "pollinations-enter";
     5	
     6	/** Run a single GraphQL query. Throws if the response carries `errors`. */
     7	export async function graphql<T>(
     8	    token: string,
     9	    query: string,
    10	    variables: Record<string, unknown>,
    11	): Promise<T> {
    12	    const res = await fetch(`${GITHUB_API}/graphql`, {
    13	        method: "POST",
    14	        headers: {
    15	            Authorization: `token ${token}`,
    16	            "User-Agent": USER_AGENT,
    17	            "Content-Type": "application/json",
    18	        },
    19	        body: JSON.stringify({ query, variables }),
    20	    });
    21	    if (!res.ok) {
    22	        throw new Error(`GitHub GraphQL -> ${res.status}: ${await res.text()}`);
    23	    }
    24	    const body = (await res.json()) as { data?: T; errors?: unknown };
    25	    if (body.errors) {
    26	        throw new Error(
    27	            `GitHub GraphQL errors: ${JSON.stringify(body.errors)}`,
    28	        );
    29	    }
    30	    if (!body.data) {
    31	        throw new Error("GitHub GraphQL returned no data");
    32	    }
    33	    return body.data;
    34	}
===== shared/gpu-registry.ts =====
     1	export type GpuServerEntry = {
     2	    url: string;
     3	    lastHeartbeat: number;
     4	    // Last observed /generate latency, used by Gen's weighted routing.
     5	    lastMs?: number;
     6	};
     7	
     8	export const gpuServerPrefix = (environment: string, type: string): string =>
     9	    `image:server:${environment}:${type}:`;
    10	
    11	// Separate from heartbeat writes so they cannot clobber latency samples.
    12	export const gpuLatencyKey = (
    13	    environment: string,
    14	    type: string,
    15	    hash: string,
    16	): string => `image:latency:${environment}:${type}:${hash}`;
    17	
    18	// Routing and monitoring must agree on which registered GPUs are live.
    19	export async function readGpuServers(
    20	    kv: KVNamespace,
    21	    environment: string,
    22	    type: string,
    23	): Promise<GpuServerEntry[]> {
    24	    const prefix = gpuServerPrefix(environment, type);
    25	    const { keys } = await kv.list({ prefix });
    26	    const now = Date.now();
    27	    const entries = await Promise.all(
    28	        keys.map(async (key) => {
    29	            const entry = await kv.get<GpuServerEntry>(key.name, "json");
    30	            if (!entry || now - entry.lastHeartbeat >= 180_000) return null;
    31	            const hash = key.name.slice(prefix.length);
    32	            const lastMs = await kv.get<number>(
    33	                gpuLatencyKey(environment, type, hash),
    34	                "json",
    35	            );
    36	            return lastMs != null ? { ...entry, lastMs } : entry;
    37	        }),
    38	    );
    39	    return entries.filter((entry): entry is GpuServerEntry => entry !== null);
    40	}

===== shared/http/fix-link.ts =====
     1	import type { AgentRunClaims } from "../auth/agent-run-token.ts";
     2	import type { AuthenticatedApiKey } from "../auth/api-key.ts";
     3	import { PUBLIC_URLS } from "../public-urls.ts";
     4	
     5	/**
     6	 * Refusals the key's owner can fix. Each one links the enter page that fixes
     7	 * it, and the same link goes into the error message, the JSON `fixUrl` and the
     8	 * chat reply.
     9	 */
    10	export type RefusalContext = {
    11	    env: {
    12	        ENVIRONMENT?: string;
    13	        BETTER_AUTH_SECRET: string;
    14	        BETTER_AUTH_URL?: string;
    15	    };
    16	    var: {
    17	        auth?: {
    18	            apiKey?: AuthenticatedApiKey;
    19	            agentRun?: AgentRunClaims;
    20	            /** The app to return to after the fix. */
    21	            appOrigin?: string;
    22	        };
    23	    };
    24	};
    25	
    26	export const AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED_MESSAGE =
    27	    "A valid API key is required. Get one at https://enter.pollinations.ai/keys, or buy one with USDC (x402) at https://enter.pollinations.ai/api/x402/keys";
    28	
    29	/** A link to an enter page on the environment that matches this worker. */
    30	export function fixLink(
    31	    c: RefusalContext,
    32	    path: string,
    33	    params: Record<string, string | undefined>,
    34	): string {
    35	    // Enter links to its own origin; gen picks the enter of its environment.
    36	    // app.request() tests run without env.
    37	    const base =
    38	        c.env?.BETTER_AUTH_URL ??
    39	        (c.env?.ENVIRONMENT === "staging"
    40	            ? PUBLIC_URLS.enter.staging
    41	            : PUBLIC_URLS.enter.production);
    42	    const url = new URL(path, base);
    43	    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries({
    44	        ...params,
    45	        redirect: c.var.auth?.appOrigin,
    46	    })) {
    47	        if (value) url.searchParams.set(key, value);
    48	    }
    49	    return url.toString();
    50	}

===== shared/http/permission-required-error.ts =====
     1	import { HTTPException } from "hono/http-exception";
     2	import { type Grant, signGrantAgent } from "../auth/agent-run-token.ts";
     3	import { fixLink, type RefusalContext } from "./fix-link.ts";
     4	
     5	/** The key lacks a model or account permission its owner can grant at `fixUrl`. */
     6	export class PermissionRequiredError extends HTTPException {
     7	    constructor(
     8	        message: string,
     9	        readonly fixUrl: string,
    10	    ) {
    11	        super(403, { message });
    12	    }
    13	}
    14	
    15	export function permissionRequired(
    16	    c: RefusalContext,
    17	    grant: Grant,
    18	    reason: string,
    19	): PermissionRequiredError {
    20	    const id = c.var.auth?.apiKey?.id ?? "";
    21	    // During an agent run, sign the agent's name into the link so the grant
    22	    // page can show who asked without trusting the agent to name itself.
    23	    const agent = c.var.auth?.agentRun?.agentModelId;
    24	    const sig =
    25	        agent &&
    26	        signGrantAgent({
    27	            secret: c.env.BETTER_AUTH_SECRET,
    28	            apiKeyId: id,
    29	            grant,
    30	            agent,
    31	        });
    32	    const fixUrl = fixLink(c, "/grant", {
    33	        id,
    34	        ...grant,
    35	        agent,
    36	        sig,
    37	        ref: "agent_grant",
    38	    });
    39	    return new PermissionRequiredError(
    40	        `${reason} Allow it at ${fixUrl}`,
    41	        fixUrl,
    42	    );
    43	}

===== shared/image-mime.ts =====
     1	export type ImageMimeType =
     2	    | "image/png"
     3	    | "image/jpeg"
     4	    | "image/webp"
     5	    | "image/gif"
     6	    | "image/bmp";
     7	
     8	export function detectImageMimeType(bytes: Uint8Array): ImageMimeType | null {
     9	    if (
    10	        bytes[0] === 0x89 &&
    11	        bytes[1] === 0x50 &&
    12	        bytes[2] === 0x4e &&
    13	        bytes[3] === 0x47
    14	    ) {
    15	        return "image/png";
    16	    }
    17	    if (bytes[0] === 0xff && bytes[1] === 0xd8 && bytes[2] === 0xff) {
    18	        return "image/jpeg";
    19	    }
    20	    if (
    21	        bytes[0] === 0x52 &&
    22	        bytes[1] === 0x49 &&
    23	        bytes[2] === 0x46 &&
    24	        bytes[3] === 0x46 &&
    25	        bytes[8] === 0x57 &&
    26	        bytes[9] === 0x45 &&
    27	        bytes[10] === 0x42 &&
    28	        bytes[11] === 0x50
    29	    ) {
    30	        return "image/webp";
    31	    }
    32	    if (bytes[0] === 0x47 && bytes[1] === 0x49 && bytes[2] === 0x46) {
    33	        return "image/gif";
    34	    }
    35	    if (bytes[0] === 0x42 && bytes[1] === 0x4d) return "image/bmp";
    36	    return null;
    37	}
===== shared/logger.ts =====
     1	import { AsyncLocalStorage } from "node:async_hooks";
     2	import { inspect } from "node:util";
     3	import {
     4	    configure,
     5	    type FormattedValues,
     6	    getAnsiColorFormatter,
     7	    getConsoleSink,
     8	    getJsonLinesFormatter,
     9	    type LogLevel,
    10	} from "@logtape/logtape";
    11	import { applyColor } from "./util.ts";
    12	
    13	export type LogFormat = "json" | "text";
    14	
    15	function formatValue(v: unknown): string {
    16	    if (typeof v === "string") return v;
    17	    else return inspect(v, { colors: true, compact: false });
    18	}
    19	
    20	function formatLogline(vs: FormattedValues): string {
    21	    const requestId = vs.record.properties["requestId"];
    22	    const shortRequestId =
    23	        typeof requestId === "string"
    24	            ? applyColor("cyan", `[${requestId.slice(0, 8)}]`)
    25	            : undefined;
    26	    return [vs.level, shortRequestId, vs.category, vs.message]
    27	        .filter((v) => !!v)
    28	        .join(" ");
    29	}
    30	
    31	let configured = false;
    32	
    33	const jsonLinesFormatter = () =>
    34	    getJsonLinesFormatter({
    35	        properties: "nest:properties",
    36	        categorySeparator: ":",
    37	    });
    38	
    39	const ansiColorFormatter = () =>
    40	    getAnsiColorFormatter({
    41	        level: "FULL",
    42	        value: formatValue,
    43	        format: formatLogline,
    44	    });
    45	
    46	export async function ensureConfigured(options: {
    47	    level: LogLevel;
    48	    format?: LogFormat;
    49	}) {
    50	    if (configured) return;
    51	    await configure({
    52	        sinks: {
    53	            console: getConsoleSink({
    54	                formatter:
    55	                    options.format === "json"
    56	                        ? jsonLinesFormatter()
    57	                        : ansiColorFormatter(),
    58	            }),
    59	        },
    60	        loggers: [
    61	            {
    62	                category: ["logtape", "meta"],
    63	                sinks: ["console"],
    64	                lowestLevel: "warning",
    65	            },
    66	            {
    67	                category: [], // catches all categories
    68	                sinks: ["console"],
    69	                lowestLevel: options.level,
    70	            },
    71	        ],
    72	        contextLocalStorage: new AsyncLocalStorage(),
    73	        reset: true,
    74	    });
    75	    configured = true;
    76	}
===== shared/mcp-usage.ts =====
     1	import { MCP_USAGE_HEADERS } from "./registry/mcp.ts";
     2	
     3	export type McpUsageReceipt = {
     4	    cost: number;
     5	    tool: string;
     6	    status: number;
     7	    adjustmentId: string;
     8	    adjustmentUnits: number;
     9	    error?: string;
    10	};
    11	
    12	export function parseMcpUsageHeaders(
    13	    headers: Headers,
    14	): McpUsageReceipt | undefined {
    15	    const costHeader = headers.get(MCP_USAGE_HEADERS.cost);
    16	    if (costHeader === null) return undefined;
    17	
    18	    const receipt = {
    19	        cost: Number(costHeader),
    20	        status: Number(headers.get(MCP_USAGE_HEADERS.status)),
    21	        adjustmentUnits: Number(headers.get(MCP_USAGE_HEADERS.adjustmentUnits)),
    22	        tool: headers.get(MCP_USAGE_HEADERS.tool),
    23	        adjustmentId: headers.get(MCP_USAGE_HEADERS.adjustmentId),
    24	        error: headers.get(MCP_USAGE_HEADERS.error) ?? undefined,
    25	    };
    26	    if (
    27	        !Number.isFinite(receipt.cost) ||
    28	        receipt.cost < 0 ||
    29	        !Number.isInteger(receipt.status) ||
    30	        receipt.status < 100 ||
    31	        receipt.status > 599 ||
    32	        !Number.isFinite(receipt.adjustmentUnits) ||
    33	        receipt.adjustmentUnits < 0 ||
    34	        !receipt.tool ||
    35	        !receipt.adjustmentId
    36	    ) {
    37	        throw new Error("MCP server returned invalid usage metadata");
    38	    }
    39	    return receipt as McpUsageReceipt;
    40	}
    41	
    42	export function withMcpUsageHeaders(
    43	    response: Response,
    44	    receipt: McpUsageReceipt | undefined,
    45	): Response {
    46	    if (!receipt) return response;
    47	    const result = new Response(response.body, response);
    48	    result.headers.set(MCP_USAGE_HEADERS.cost, String(receipt.cost));
    49	    result.headers.set(MCP_USAGE_HEADERS.tool, receipt.tool);
    50	    result.headers.set(MCP_USAGE_HEADERS.status, String(receipt.status));
    51	    result.headers.set(MCP_USAGE_HEADERS.adjustmentId, receipt.adjustmentId);
    52	    result.headers.set(
    53	        MCP_USAGE_HEADERS.adjustmentUnits,
    54	        String(receipt.adjustmentUnits),
    55	    );
    56	    if (receipt.error) {
    57	        result.headers.set(
    58	            MCP_USAGE_HEADERS.error,
    59	            receipt.error.replace(/[\r\n]+/g, " ").slice(0, 1000),
    60	        );
    61	    }
    62	    return result;
    63	}
===== shared/middleware/logger.ts =====
     1	import {
     2	    getLogger,
     3	    type Logger,
     4	    type LogLevel,
     5	    withContext,
     6	} from "@logtape/logtape";
     7	import { createMiddleware } from "hono/factory";
     8	import { getRealClientIp } from "../client-ip.ts";
     9	import { ensureConfigured, type LogFormat } from "../logger.ts";
    10	import { redactCredentialQueryParams } from "../observability/request-inputs.ts";
    11	import { getPublicUrl } from "../public-origin.ts";
    12	
    13	export type LoggerVariables = {
    14	    log: Logger;
    15	    requestStartedAt: number;
    16	};
    17	
    18	type Env = {
    19	    Bindings: {
    20	        LOG_LEVEL?: LogLevel;
    21	        LOG_FORMAT?: LogFormat;
    22	        ENVIRONMENT?: string;
    23	    };
    24	    Variables: LoggerVariables & { requestId?: string };
    25	};
    26	
    27	export const logger = createMiddleware<Env>(async (c, next) => {
    28	    await ensureConfigured({
    29	        level: c.env.LOG_LEVEL || "debug",
    30	        format: c.env.LOG_FORMAT || "text",
    31	    });
    32	    const log = getLogger(["hono"]);
    33	    c.set("log", log);
    34	
    35	    const startTime = Date.now();
    36	    c.set("requestStartedAt", startTime);
    37	    const shouldEmitRequestLogs =
    38	        c.env.ENVIRONMENT === "local" || c.env.ENVIRONMENT === "test";
    39	
    40	    const publicUrl = redactCredentialQueryParams(getPublicUrl(c));
    41	
    42	    await withContext(
    43	        {
    44	            requestId: c.var.requestId,
    45	            method: c.req.method,
    46	            routePath: publicUrl,
    47	            userAgent: c.req.header("user-agent"),
    48	            ipAddress: getRealClientIp(c),
    49	        },
    50	        async () => {
    51	            if (shouldEmitRequestLogs) {
    52	                log.info("{method} {url}", {
    53	                    method: c.req.method,
    54	                    url: publicUrl,
    55	                });
    56	            }
    57	
    58	            await next();
    59	
    60	            const duration = Date.now() - startTime;
    61	            if (shouldEmitRequestLogs) {
    62	                log.info("RESPONSE {status} {duration}ms", {
    63	                    status: c.res.status,
    64	                    duration,
    65	                });
    66	            }
    67	        },
    68	    );
    69	});
===== shared/middleware/request-id.ts =====
     1	import type { MiddlewareHandler } from "hono";
     2	import type { RequestIdVariables } from "hono/request-id";
     3	
     4	const HEADER_NAME = "X-Request-Id";
     5	
     6	/**
     7	 * Mints a fresh request id server-side on every request. Unlike hono's
     8	 * `requestId()`, this never trusts an inbound `X-Request-Id` header — a
     9	 * client-supplied id let callers pin/replay ids (see #12889), corrupting
    10	 * anything keyed on request_id (e.g. S3 output paths, fallback-attempt
    11	 * grouping). The response header is still set so callers can read the id.
    12	 */
    13	export const requestId = (): MiddlewareHandler<{
    14	    Variables: RequestIdVariables;
    15	}> => {
    16	    return async (c, next) => {
    17	        const id = crypto.randomUUID();
    18	        c.set("requestId", id);
    19	        c.header(HEADER_NAME, id);
    20	        await next();
    21	    };
    22	};
===== shared/middleware/validator.ts =====
     1	import type { ValidationTargets } from "hono";
     2	import { validator as zValidator } from "hono-openapi";
     3	import { ZodError, type z } from "zod";
     4	import type { $ZodIssue } from "zod/v4/core";
     5	import {
     6	    ValidationError,
     7	    type ValidationTarget,
     8	} from "../http/validation-error.ts";
     9	
    10	export const validator = <
    11	    T extends z.ZodType,
    12	    Target extends keyof ValidationTargets,
    13	>(
    14	    target: Target,
    15	    schema: T,
    16	) =>
    17	    zValidator(target, schema, (result, _c) => {
    18	        if (!result.success) {
    19	            throw new ValidationError(
    20	                new ZodError(result.error as $ZodIssue[]),
    21	                target as ValidationTarget,
    22	            );
    23	        }
    24	    });
===== shared/model-health.ts =====
     1	// Shared rollup shape for catalog reliability and time-window diagnostics.
     2	// Rollup rows count what callers experienced after fallbacks, not attempts.
     3	export type ModelHealthRow = {
     4	    model?: string;
     5	    event_type?: string;
     6	    is_rollup?: number | boolean;
     7	    status_2xx?: number;
     8	    errors_5xx?: number;
     9	};
    10	
    11	export type ModelHealthStatus = "healthy" | "degraded" | "down" | "unknown";
    12	
    13	export type ModelHealth = {
    14	    status: ModelHealthStatus;
    15	    requests: number;
    16	    /** Percentage of 2xx among 2xx + 5xx, or null without requests. */
    17	    successRate: number | null;
    18	};
    19	
    20	// Diagnostic colors are independent of the >80% community discovery cutoff.
    21	const DEGRADED_5XX_PERCENT = 5;
    22	const DOWN_5XX_PERCENT = 20;
    23	
    24	/** Discovery is fail-open when there are no recent observations. */
    25	export function isModelReliable(
    26	    successRate: number | null | undefined,
    27	): boolean {
    28	    return successRate == null || successRate > 80;
    29	}
    30	
    31	/** Health per model id and category (`text`, `image`, ...) from rollup rows. */
    32	export function modelHealthLookup(
    33	    rows: ModelHealthRow[],
    34	): (model: string, category: string) => ModelHealth {
    35	    const rollups = new Map(
    36	        rows
    37	            .filter((row) => row.is_rollup)
    38	            .map((row) => [`${row.model}\0${row.event_type}`, row]),
    39	    );
    40	    return (model, category) =>
    41	        modelHealthFromRow(rollups.get(`${model}\0generate.${category}`));
    42	}
    43	
    44	function modelHealthFromRow(row: ModelHealthRow | undefined): ModelHealth {
    45	    const success = row?.status_2xx ?? 0;
    46	    const errors5xx = row?.errors_5xx ?? 0;
    47	    const requests = success + errors5xx;
    48	    if (requests === 0) {
    49	        return { status: "unknown", requests: 0, successRate: null };
    50	    }
    51	    const percent5xx = (errors5xx / requests) * 100;
    52	    const status =
    53	        percent5xx >= DOWN_5XX_PERCENT
    54	            ? "down"
    55	            : percent5xx >= DEGRADED_5XX_PERCENT
    56	              ? "degraded"
    57	              : "healthy";
    58	    return { status, requests, successRate: (success / requests) * 100 };
    59	}
===== shared/observability/request-inputs.ts =====
     1	import type { Context } from "hono";
     2	
     3	export type RequestInputs = {
     4	    params?: Record<string, string>;
     5	    query?: Record<string, string | string[]>;
     6	    body?: unknown;
     7	};
     8	
     9	const BODY_METHODS = new Set(["POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE"]);
    10	const CREDENTIAL_QUERY_PARAMS = new Set([
    11	    "access_token",
    12	    "accesstoken",
    13	    "api_key",
    14	    "apikey",
    15	    "authorization",
    16	    "bearer_token",
    17	    "bearertoken",
    18	    "headers",
    19	    "key",
    20	    "token",
    21	]);
    22	const REDACTED = "[redacted]";
    23	
    24	export function redactCredentialQueryParams(url: URL): string {
    25	    const redacted = new URL(url);
    26	    for (const param of redacted.searchParams.keys()) {
    27	        if (CREDENTIAL_QUERY_PARAMS.has(param.toLowerCase())) {
    28	            redacted.searchParams.set(param, REDACTED);
    29	        }
    30	    }
    31	    return redacted.toString();
    32	}
    33	
    34	export async function collectRequestInputs(c: Context): Promise<RequestInputs> {
    35	    const inputs: RequestInputs = {
    36	        params: removeEmptyRecord(safeParams(c)),
    37	        query: removeEmptyRecord(queryParams(c)),
    38	    };
    39	
    40	    const body = await requestBody(c);
    41	    if (body !== undefined) {
    42	        inputs.body = body;
    43	    }
    44	
    45	    return removeUndefined(inputs);
    46	}
    47	
    48	// Hono's c.req.param() throws TypeError when called on a request that didn't
    49	// match any route (e.g. when an error fires before routing completes, or in
    50	// the notFound/onError handlers). Since this helper exists to enrich error
    51	// envelopes, it must never crash the error handler.
    52	function safeParams(c: Context): Record<string, string> {
    53	    try {
    54	        return c.req.param();
    55	    } catch {
    56	        return {};
    57	    }
    58	}
    59	
    60	export function stringifyRequestInputs(inputs: RequestInputs | undefined) {
    61	    try {
    62	        return JSON.stringify(inputs ?? {});
    63	    } catch (error) {
    64	        return JSON.stringify({
    65	            error: "request_inputs_json_stringify_failed",
    66	            message: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
    67	        });
    68	    }
    69	}
    70	
    71	async function requestBody(c: Context): Promise<unknown> {
    72	    if (!BODY_METHODS.has(c.req.method)) return undefined;
    73	
    74	    const contentType = c.req.header("content-type") || "";
    75	    if (!contentType) return undefined;
    76	
    77	    try {
    78	        if (contentType.includes("json")) {
    79	            return redactBodyFields(await c.req.json());
    80	        }
    81	
    82	        if (
    83	            contentType.includes("multipart/form-data") ||
    84	            contentType.includes("application/x-www-form-urlencoded")
    85	        ) {
    86	            return redactBodyFields(formDataToObject(await c.req.formData()));
    87	        }
    88	
    89	        const text = await c.req.text();
    90	        return text || undefined;
    91	    } catch (error) {
    92	        return {
    93	            error: "request_body_unavailable",
    94	            message: error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error),
    95	        };
    96	    }
    97	}
    98	
    99	function queryParams(c: Context): Record<string, string | string[]> {
   100	    return Object.fromEntries(
   101	        Object.entries(c.req.queries()).map(([key, values]) => [
   102	            key,
   103	            redactQueryParam(key, values.length === 1 ? values[0] : values),
   104	        ]),
   105	    );
   106	}
   107	
   108	function redactQueryParam(
   109	    key: string,
   110	    value: string | string[],
   111	): string | string[] {
   112	    return CREDENTIAL_QUERY_PARAMS.has(key.toLowerCase()) ? REDACTED : value;
   113	}
   114	
   115	function redactBodyFields(value: unknown): unknown {
   116	    if (Array.isArray(value)) {
   117	        return value.map(redactBodyFields);
   118	    }
   119	
   120	    if (!value || typeof value !== "object") {
   121	        return value;
   122	    }
   123	
   124	    return Object.fromEntries(
   125	        Object.entries(value).map(([key, fieldValue]) => [
   126	            key,
   127	            CREDENTIAL_QUERY_PARAMS.has(key.toLowerCase())
   128	                ? REDACTED
   129	                : redactBodyFields(fieldValue),
   130	        ]),
   131	    );
   132	}
   133	
   134	function formDataToObject(formData: FormData): Record<string, unknown> {
   135	    const result: Record<string, unknown> = {};
   136	
   137	    for (const [key, value] of formData.entries()) {
   138	        const serialized =
   139	            value instanceof File
   140	                ? {
   141	                      name: value.name,
   142	                      size: value.size,
   143	                      type: value.type,
   144	                  }
   145	                : value;
   146	
   147	        const existing = result[key];
   148	        if (existing === undefined) {
   149	            result[key] = serialized;
   150	        } else if (Array.isArray(existing)) {
   151	            existing.push(serialized);
   152	        } else {
   153	            result[key] = [existing, serialized];
   154	        }
   155	    }
   156	
   157	    return result;
   158	}
   159	
   160	function removeEmptyRecord<T extends Record<string, unknown>>(
   161	    record: T,
   162	): T | undefined {
   163	    return Object.keys(record).length ? record : undefined;
   164	}
   165	
   166	function removeUndefined<T extends Record<string, unknown>>(record: T): T {
   167	    return Object.fromEntries(
   168	        Object.entries(record).filter(([, value]) => value !== undefined),
   169	    ) as T;
   170	}

===== shared/providers.ts =====
     1	/** Resolve explicit vendor IDs and aliases; unknown names stay unresolved. */
     2	export function createProviderResolver<
     3	    T extends { id: string; aliases: readonly string[] },
     4	>(providers: readonly T[]) {
     5	    const byName = new Map<string, T>();
     6	    for (const provider of providers) {
     7	        for (const name of [provider.id, ...provider.aliases]) {
     8	            byName.set(name, provider);
     9	        }
    10	    }
    11	    return (value: string): T | undefined =>
    12	        byName.get(value.trim().toLowerCase());
    13	}

     6	 * headers are ignored: nothing sits in front of the Workers to set them (#17462).
     7	 */
     8	export function getPublicOrigin(c: Context): string {

    10	}

    33	// Myceli is the upstream — never reached directly by end users — so absolute
    34	// URLs baked into Stripe checkout, OAuth redirects, and email links must use
    35	// the Pollinations profile.
    36	export const ACTIVE_PUBLIC_URL_PROFILE =
    37	    "pollinations" satisfies PublicUrlProfile;
    38	export const PUBLIC_URLS = PUBLIC_URL_PROFILES[ACTIVE_PUBLIC_URL_PROFILE];
    39	
    40	export const AUTH_TRUSTED_ORIGINS = Object.values(PUBLIC_URL_PROFILES).flatMap(
    41	    ({ root, wildcard }) => [root, wildcard],
    42	);
===== shared/r2-storage.ts =====
     1	const R2_LIFECYCLE_TTL_MS = 30 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000;
     2	
     3	export const DEFAULT_R2_TTL_REFRESH_AGE_MS = R2_LIFECYCLE_TTL_MS / 2;
     4	
     5	type RefreshR2ObjectTtlOptions = {
     6	    minRefreshAgeMs?: number;
     7	    now?: () => Date;
     8	};
     9	
    10	async function writeReadableToWritable(
    11	    readable: ReadableStream<Uint8Array>,
    12	    writable: WritableStream<ArrayBuffer | ArrayBufferView>,
    13	): Promise<void> {
    14	    const reader = readable.getReader();
    15	    const writer = writable.getWriter();
    16	
    17	    try {
    18	        while (true) {
    19	            const { done, value } = await reader.read();
    20	            if (done) break;
    21	            await writer.write(value);
    22	        }
    23	        await writer.close();
    24	    } catch (error) {
    25	        await writer.abort(error).catch(() => undefined);
    26	        throw error;
    27	    } finally {
    28	        reader.releaseLock();
    29	        writer.releaseLock();
    30	    }
    31	}
    32	
    33	export function refreshR2ObjectTtl(
    34	    bucket: R2Bucket,
    35	    key: string,
    36	    object: R2ObjectBody,
    37	    waitUntil: (promise: Promise<unknown>) => void,
    38	    onError: (error: unknown) => void,
    39	    options: RefreshR2ObjectTtlOptions = {},
    40	): ReadableStream {
    41	    const minRefreshAgeMs =
    42	        options.minRefreshAgeMs ?? DEFAULT_R2_TTL_REFRESH_AGE_MS;
    43	    const ageMs =
    44	        (options.now?.() ?? new Date()).getTime() - object.uploaded.getTime();
    45	
    46	    // R2 has no metadata-only touch; rewriting resets lifecycle age but is a
    47	    // Class A write, so refresh only after half of the fixed 30-day lifecycle.
    48	    if (ageMs < minRefreshAgeMs) {
    49	        return object.body;
    50	    }
    51	
    52	    const [responseBody, refreshBody] = object.body.tee();
    53	    const fixedLengthStream = new FixedLengthStream(object.size);
    54	
    55	    waitUntil(
    56	        Promise.all([
    57	            writeReadableToWritable(
    58	                refreshBody as ReadableStream<Uint8Array>,
    59	                fixedLengthStream.writable,
    60	            ),
    61	            bucket.put(key, fixedLengthStream.readable, {
    62	                httpMetadata: object.httpMetadata,
    63	                customMetadata: object.customMetadata,
    64	                storageClass: object.storageClass,
    65	                // Rewrite only while the object is still these exact bytes:
    66	                // a concurrent delete (or replacement) must win, or the
    67	                // refresh would silently resurrect an object that can no
    68	                // longer be deleted through any API.
    69	                onlyIf: { etagMatches: object.etag },
    70	            }),
    71	        ])
    72	            .then(() => undefined)
    73	            .catch(onError),
    74	    );
    75	
    76	    return responseBody;
    77	}
===== shared/rate-limit.ts =====
     1	import type { Context } from "hono";
     2	import { createMiddleware } from "hono/factory";
     3	import { HTTPException } from "hono/http-exception";
     4	import { extractApiKey } from "./auth/api-key.ts";
     5	import { bytesToHex, getRealClientIp } from "./client-ip.ts";
     6	
     7	type RateLimitEnv = {
     8	    Bindings: {
     9	        EDGE_RATE_LIMITER?: RateLimit;
    10	        EDGE_IP_RATE_LIMITER?: RateLimit;
    11	    };
    12	};
    13	
    14	/**
    15	 * Cloudflare-native limit that runs before auth, so one flooding key is
    16	 * rejected without reaching D1. Counts per API key, hashed so no lookup is
    17	 * needed. With `byIp`, requests without a key count per client IP instead,
    18	 * and keyed requests also count per IP in `EDGE_IP_RATE_LIMITER`, so
    19	 * rotating made-up keys from one IP cannot dodge the limit. Each Worker's
    20	 * wrangler.toml sets its limits per 10 seconds, matching `Retry-After`.
    21	 * Enter leaves `byIp` off because gen's internal calls arrive without a
    22	 * client IP; it still counts every request that carries a client IP, keyed
    23	 * or not, so public routes such as device codes, app lookup and sign-in
    24	 * cannot be flooded into D1 with made-up keys. Cloudflare counts per
    25	 * location, so this caps floods rather than enforcing an exact quota.
    26	 */
    27	export function rateLimit({ byIp }: { byIp: boolean }) {
    28	    return createMiddleware<RateLimitEnv>(async (c, next) => {
    29	        const apiKey = extractApiKey(c.req.raw);
    30	        const ip = `ip:${getRealClientIp(c)}`;
    31	        if (apiKey) {
    32	            const digest = await crypto.subtle.digest(
    33	                "SHA-256",
    34	                new TextEncoder().encode(apiKey),
    35	            );
    36	            await limit(
    37	                c,
    38	                c.env.EDGE_RATE_LIMITER,
    39	                `key:${bytesToHex(digest)}`,
    40	            );
    41	            if (byIp) await limit(c, c.env.EDGE_IP_RATE_LIMITER, ip);
    42	        } else if (byIp) {
    43	            await limit(c, c.env.EDGE_RATE_LIMITER, ip);
    44	        }
    45	        if (!byIp && c.req.header("cf-connecting-ip")) {
    46	            await limit(c, c.env.EDGE_RATE_LIMITER, ip);
    47	        }
    48	        await next();
    49	    });
    50	}
    51	
    52	/** A 429 once `key` is over `limiter`; `retryAfter` is its period in seconds. */
    53	export async function limit(
    54	    c: Context,
    55	    limiter: RateLimit | undefined,
    56	    key: string,
    57	    retryAfter = 10,
    58	) {
    59	    if (limiter && !(await limiter.limit({ key })).success) {
    60	        c.header("Retry-After", String(retryAfter));
    61	        throw new HTTPException(429, {
    62	            message: "Too many requests. Please slow down.",
    63	        });
    64	    }
    65	}
